definition_zh: 侄子；外甥；姻亲的侄甥；旧指孙子、后裔
definition_en: the son of your brother or sister, or of your husband's or wife's sibling; in older use, a male descendant
core_image: 院门口的葡萄架下放着一只旧行李箱，一个半大男孩站在门廊上等长辈开口
scene: 暑假第一天的傍晚，院门口的葡萄架下放着一只旧行李箱，男孩正和长辈打招呼。My nephew will stay with us for three weeks this summer.
sceneCN: 这里是「侄子／外甥」（第 1 个义项：兄弟姐妹的儿子）；句意为我的侄子这个夏天要在我们这儿住三个星期。图中可辨识物件：葡萄架、旧行李箱、门廊。

pos.zh: 侄子；外甥；姻亲的侄甥；旧指孙子、后裔

derivatives.zh: 与 nephew 同出拉丁亲属词，是阴性对应词，义为「侄女；外甥女」
由拉丁词干 nepot-（侄子、孙子）加 -ism 构成，义为「任人唯亲」
由 nepotism 加 -ic 构成，义为「任人唯亲的；偏袒亲属的」

senses.title: The son of your brother or sister
senses.definition: a boy or man who is the son of your brother or sister
senses.definitionCN: 兄弟姐妹的儿子
senses.example: My nephew will stay with us for three weeks this summer.
senses.exampleCN: 我的侄子这个夏天要在我们这儿住三个星期。
senses.why: Latin nepos covered both grandson and nephew, so English inherited one word for a young male kinsman one generation below the speaker, without asking which parent supplied the link.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nepos 同时指孙子和侄子，英语因此只继承了一个词，用来指比自己低一辈的男性亲属，并不追问是哪位长辈带来的这层关系。

senses.title: The son of your spouse's sibling
senses.titleCN: 姻亲的侄甥；配偶那边的侄子
senses.definition: the son of your husband's or wife's brother or sister, related by marriage rather than by blood
senses.definitionCN: 丈夫或妻子的兄弟姐妹的儿子，靠婚姻而非血缘联系起来
senses.example: Her nephew came to the wedding with his parents.
senses.exampleCN: 她的侄子跟着父母来参加了婚礼。
senses.why: Marriage folds two family trees together, and English simply applies the existing kinship word to the partner's side, so no new form is needed for a nephew acquired through a spouse.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻把两棵家族树并到一起，英语直接把已有的亲属词用到伴侣那一边，所以因配偶而得到的侄子并不需要另造一个词。

senses.title: A male descendant, in older usage
senses.definition: in older texts, a grandson or any male descendant, not only a sibling's son
senses.definitionCN: 旧时文本中指孙子或任何男性后裔，而不只指兄弟姐妹的儿子
senses.example: In the old chronicle, the king named his nephew as heir.
senses.exampleCN: 在那部旧编年史里，国王指定他的孙子为继承人。
senses.why: The Latin word meant grandson before it meant nephew, and early English kept that wider sense until grandson and cousin took over the narrower jobs and left nephew with its modern range.
senses.whyCN: 这个拉丁词先指孙子，后指侄子；早期英语保留了较宽的意思，直到 grandson 与 cousin 接走那些更窄的职责，才把 nephew 留在今天的范围里。

intro.en: Nephew goes back to a Latin word that named a grandson as well as a nephew, and it reached English through French with its family range already narrowed.
intro.cn: nephew 可追到既指孙子又指侄子的拉丁词，经法语进入英语时，它的亲属范围已经收窄。

items.en: Nepos meant a grandson and also a nephew, and its stem nepot- survives in words about favour shown to relatives.
items.cn: nepos 既指孙子也指侄子，其词干 nepot- 留在表示「偏袒亲属」的词里。

items.en: Neptis was the matching feminine noun for a granddaughter, and it is the source of the English word for a sibling's daughter.
items.cn: neptis 是相配的阴性名词，指孙女，也是英语中「侄女、外甥女」一词的来源。

items.en: Old French narrowed the Latin word to neveu, the son of a sibling, and passed the form to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语把拉丁词收窄为 neveu，专指兄弟姐妹的儿子，并在诺曼时期之后传入英语。

items.en: Middle English wrote the word as neveu or nevew, and spellings with ph appeared later under the influence of the Latin stem nepot-.
items.cn: 中古英语写作 neveu 或 nevew，带 ph 的拼写是后来受拉丁词干 nepot- 影响才出现的。

items.en: Modern English keeps nephew for a sibling's son, adds the in-law sense, and leaves the older grandson sense to historical writing.
items.cn: 现代英语用 nephew 指兄弟姐妹的儿子，添上姻亲义，把较旧的「孙子」义留给历史写作。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the learned words built on the same Latin stem of kinship; the near-meaning group holds the other names for close family members.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁亲属词干上造出的书面词；近义组收其他表示近亲称谓的词。

entries.definition: The practice of giving jobs or favours to relatives, built on the Latin stem for nephew.
entries.definitionCN: 把职位或好处给亲属的做法，建在表示「侄子」的拉丁词干上。

entries.definition: A person who favours relatives in appointments or business.
entries.definitionCN: 在任用或生意中偏袒亲属的人。

entries.definition: Showing favouritism towards relatives, formed from nepotism with -ic.
entries.definitionCN: 表现出对亲属偏袒的，由 nepotism 加 -ic 构成。

entries.definition: The daughter of your brother or sister, the female counterpart of nephew.
entries.definitionCN: 兄弟姐妹的女儿，是 nephew 的阴性对应词。

entries.definition: The child of your aunt or uncle, another kinsman of your own generation.
entries.definitionCN: 姑舅姨伯的孩子，同辈的另一类亲属。

entries.definition: A person connected to you by blood or marriage, the general term above nephew.
entries.definitionCN: 因血缘或婚姻与你相连的人，是覆盖 nephew 的上位词。

entries.definition: A male relative, used in older or literary English.
entries.definitionCN: 男性亲属，多用于较旧或文学性的英语。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin kinship noun that French narrowed, and its relatives keep the same picture of a younger male in the family.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是法语收窄过的拉丁亲属名词，它的同族词都保留着「家族中较年幼男性」的画面。

normal.en: Latin nepos meant both grandson and nephew, so the English word started with a wider family range than it now has.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nepos 兼指孙子与侄子，所以英语这个词一开始的亲属范围比现在宽。

normal.en: French reduced the Latin word to neveu, and English respelled it with ph because the Latin stem nepot- was still visible in learned words.
normal.cn: 法语把拉丁词缩成 neveu，英语又用 ph 改写，因为拉丁词干 nepot- 在书面词里仍然看得见。

normal.en: Niece is the matching word from Latin neptis, so nephew and niece are two branches of one Latin family rather than unrelated labels.
normal.cn: niece 是来自拉丁语 neptis 的对应词，所以 nephew 与 niece 是同一拉丁词族的两支，而不是两个互不相干的称呼。

normal.en: Nepotism comes from the same stem: favour handed to a nephew is the literal picture behind the modern word for favouritism.
normal.cn: nepotism 出自同一词干：把好处递给侄子，正是现代「任人唯亲」一词背后的字面画面。

normal.en: The in-law sense needs no new form, because English simply applies the existing kinship word to the spouse's side of the family.
normal.cn: 姻亲义不需要新形式，因为英语直接把已有的亲属词用到配偶那一边的家族。

abstract.en: A single Latin word once held a grandson and a nephew, and English kept the narrower half that everyday family life needed.
abstract.cn: 一个拉丁词曾同时装下孙子和侄子，英语只留下日常家庭生活更需要的窄的那一半。

abstract.en: A word for a boy in the family turns into a word for favouritism, because the nearest relative is also the easiest person to help.
abstract.cn: 一个指家族男孩的词变成了「任人唯亲」，因为最近的亲属也往往是最容易帮的人。

abstract.en: Nephew and niece are mirror images from one old stem, which is why the pair sounds balanced even though the endings differ.
abstract.cn: nephew 与 niece 是同一个古老词干的两面镜子，所以这对词尽管词尾不同，听起来仍然对称。

examples.en: My nephew is learning to ride a bicycle.
examples.cn: 我的侄子正在学骑自行车。

examples.en: She brought her nephew to the family dinner.
examples.cn: 她把侄子带来参加家庭聚餐。

examples.en: Their nephew by marriage stayed for the whole holiday.
examples.cn: 他们姻亲那边的侄子整个假期都住在他们家。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「涅夫尤」——叔伯家的男孩来了，喊一声就去开门；nephew 就是侄子、外甥。

root: 拉丁语 nepos（孙子；侄子，词干 nepot-）经古法语 neveu 进入英语；同族词 niece 来自拉丁语 neptis，nepotism 也出自同一词干。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a younger male kinsman; the senses then separate by blood, by marriage, and by the older use that still included grandsons.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是比自己低一辈的男性亲属；义项随后按血缘、按婚姻，以及仍包含孙子的旧用法分开。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a boy with a suitcase standing under a grape trellis, waiting for an older relative to speak.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个提着行李箱的男孩站在葡萄架下，等长辈先开口。

branches.en: a brother's son arriving with a suitcase
branches.cn: 提着行李箱到来的哥哥的儿子

branches.en: a sister's son helping in the kitchen
branches.cn: 在厨房帮忙的姐姐的儿子

branches.en: a wedding table shared by both families
branches.cn: 两家人共用的一张婚宴桌

branches.en: a partner's nephew calling at the door
branches.cn: 伴侣的侄子来敲门

branches.en: an old chronicle naming an heir
branches.cn: 旧编年史里指定继承人的那一页

intro.en: The word is carried by the Latin noun of kinship, its feminine partner, the French form that narrowed it, and the English words built on the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语亲属名词、它的阴性对应词、把它收窄的法语形式，以及同一词干上的英语词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied nepos for the male kinsman and neptis for the female counterpart, and French carried the narrowed nephew into English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了男性亲属词 nepos 与阴性对应词 neptis，法语把收窄后的 nephew 带入英语。

definition_zh: 神经；勇气；胆量；放肆；紧张不安；鼓起勇气
definition_en: a fibre that carries signals in the body; courage to do something difficult; bold rudeness; a state of nervous tension; to give oneself courage
core_image: 一根细长的白线从脊柱伸向指尖，轻轻一碰就传来一阵电流
scene: 冬天的早晨，厨房的水壶在响，母亲搓着手站在门口，声音有些发抖。I did not have the nerve to tell her the truth.
sceneCN: 这里是「胆量、勇气」（第 2 个义项：做难事所需的胆量）；句意为我没有勇气把实情告诉她。图中可辨识物件：冒着热气的水壶、门口的双手。

pos.zh: 神经；勇气；胆量；放肆；紧张不安
使鼓起勇气；给……打气

derivatives.zh: 由 nerve 加 -ous 构成，义为「紧张的；神经的」
由 nervous 加 -ly 构成，义为「紧张地；不安地」
由 nervous 加 -ness 构成，义为「紧张；神经质」
由拉丁前缀 e-（去掉）加 nervus 构成，义为「使失去活力」

senses.title: A fibre carrying signals between the brain and the body
senses.definition: a long fibre in the body that carries messages between the brain, the senses and the muscles
senses.definitionCN: 体内传递信息的长纤维，连接大脑、感官与肌肉
senses.example: The dentist damaged a nerve in my jaw.
senses.exampleCN: 牙医伤到了我下颌的一根神经。
senses.why: Latin nervus first named a sinew or tendon, the visible white cord in a body; anatomists then gave that same cord the job of carrying feeling, and the word kept the picture of a thread running through flesh.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 nervus 最初指筋或肌腱，也就是身体里看得见的白色细索；解剖学家随后让这同一根索承担传递感觉的职责，这个词便保留了「细线穿过血肉」的画面。

senses.title: Courage to face something difficult
senses.definition: the steady confidence needed to do something frightening or demanding
senses.definitionCN: 面对可怕或艰难之事时所需的稳定信心
senses.example: The climber finally lost his nerve near the summit.
senses.exampleCN: 那名登山者在接近山顶时终于失去了勇气。
senses.why: Sinews are what keep a body taut and steady, so to have nerve came to mean to hold that taut strength when fear pulls at it; courage is the sinew of the mind.
senses.whyCN: 筋让身体绷紧、稳住，因此 to have nerve 就指在恐惧拉扯时仍保持那种绷紧的力量；勇气成了心智的筋。

senses.title: Bold impudence that ignores what others expect
senses.definition: rude boldness shown by doing something others consider too cheeky
senses.definitionCN: 做出别人认为太冒失的事而显出的无礼大胆
senses.example: He had the nerve to ask for a second raise.
senses.exampleCN: 他竟厚着脸皮要求再加一次薪。
senses.why: The same strength that deserves praise can also be judged as bare-faced boldness when it ignores other people's feelings, so a word for taut power slides into a word for cheek.
senses.whyCN: 同一种值得称赞的力量，一旦无视别人的感受，也会被判为赤裸裸的放肆；于是表示「绷紧之力」的词滑成了表示「厚脸皮」的词。

senses.title: A state of nervous tension, usually in the plural
senses.definition: a feeling of being anxious and unable to relax, commonly used as the plural nerves
senses.definitionCN: 焦虑、无法放松的感觉，常用复数形式
senses.example: She had a bad case of nerves before the interview.
senses.exampleCN: 面试之前她紧张得厉害。
senses.why: Nerves were understood as the body's sensitive cords, so when those cords were overexcited the name moved from the fibres to the feeling they produced; a case of nerves is the body reporting on itself.
senses.whyCN: nerves 被理解为身体里敏感的细索，当这些索过度兴奋时，名称就从纤维转到它们产生的感觉；a case of nerves 就是身体在报告自己的状态。

senses.title: To give oneself or another person courage
senses.definition: to make oneself or someone else brave enough to do something difficult
senses.definitionCN: 使自己或别人有足够勇气去做难事
senses.example: He nerved himself to knock on the door.
senses.exampleCN: 他鼓起勇气去敲门。
senses.why: Turning the noun into a verb makes courage into a supply that can be gathered and handed over; the word changes from a thing felt in the chest to an act performed before a door.
senses.whyCN: 把名词变成动词，勇气就成了一种可以聚拢、可以递送的东西；这个词从胸腔里感到的状态，变成门前做出的动作。

intro.en: Nerve began as a Latin word for a sinew, and English stretched that cord from anatomy to courage and then to cheek, finally turning it into a verb.
intro.cn: nerve 起初是拉丁语中表示「筋」的词，英语把这条索从解剖拉到勇气、再到厚脸皮，最后还把它变成动词。

items.en: Nervus meant a sinew, tendon or cord, and Roman writers already used it for the cords running inside the body.
items.cn: nervus 意为筋、肌腱或细索，古罗马作者已用它指体内穿行的索状结构。

items.en: The adjective nervosus described something sinewy, strong and vigorous, and it is the ancestor of the English word for being tense.
items.cn: 形容词 nervosus 描述充满筋腱、强壮有力的事物，是英语中表示「紧张」那个词的祖先。

items.en: Old French nerf named a nerve or sinew and passed the word to English in the medieval period.
items.cn: 古法语 nerf 指神经或筋，在中世纪把这个词传入英语。

items.en: Middle English nerve kept the anatomical sense, while the idea of bodily strength slowly became the idea of mental courage.
items.cn: 中古英语 nerve 保留了解剖义，而「身体有力」的观念慢慢变成了「精神有胆量」。

items.en: Modern English adds the plural sense of tension, the verb of gathering courage, and the judgemental sense of bold impudence.
items.cn: 现代英语添上复数的「紧张不安」义、聚拢勇气的动词义，以及带评判意味的「放肆」义。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjectives, adverbs and verbs built on the Latin cord; the near-meaning group holds words for steadiness, boldness and the body's tough tissue.
note.cn: 形近组收建在拉丁语「索」上的形容词、副词与动词；近义组收表示镇定、大胆以及身体坚韧组织的词。

entries.definition: Anxious or easily worried; also relating to the nerves.
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑、易担忧的；也与神经有关。

entries.definition: In an anxious or fidgety manner, formed with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以焦虑或坐立不安的方式；由 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being anxious, formed with -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑、紧张的状态；由 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: To weaken or drain energy, from Latin e- plus nervus.
entries.definitionCN: 使虚弱、失去活力；来自拉丁语 e- 加 nervus。

entries.definition: The ability to face danger or pain without being stopped by fear.
entries.definitionCN: 面对危险或痛苦而不被恐惧挡住的能力。

entries.definition: Bold determination in a difficult situation, used in lively speech.
entries.definitionCN: 在困境中的大胆决心，多用于口语。

entries.definition: Bold and rude confidence that shocks other people.
entries.definitionCN: 大胆无礼、令旁人吃惊的自信。

entries.definition: A tendon or tough cord of tissue, the original bodily image of nerve.
entries.definitionCN: 肌腱或坚韧的索状组织，是 nerve 最初的身体意象。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin cord of sinew that English turned into a metaphor for courage, and its family keeps both the fibre and the feeling.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中一根筋索，英语把它变成勇气的比喻，同族词同时保留纤维与感觉两面。

normal.en: Latin nervus meant sinew or tendon, and the anatomists simply extended that visible cord to the fibres that carry feeling.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nervus 指筋或肌腱，解剖学家只是把这条看得见的索扩展到传递感觉的纤维。

normal.en: Nervous adds -ous to nerve, so it first meant full of sinew and therefore strong, not anxious.
normal.cn: nervous 是 nerve 加 -ous，最初意为「充满筋腱」因而强壮，而不是焦虑。

normal.en: To have the nerve connects courage to the tautness of sinew: a steady body is the picture behind a steady will.
normal.cn: to have the nerve 把勇气与筋的绷紧连起来：稳定的身体正是稳定意志的画面。

normal.en: The plural nerves names the fibres and also the feeling of tension, which is why a case of nerves sounds both medical and emotional.
normal.cn: 复数 nerves 既指纤维，也指紧张的感觉，所以 a case of nerves 听起来既像医学说法又像情绪描述。

normal.en: Nerve as a verb is the noun put to work: to nerve oneself is to gather the taut strength and hold it before acting.
normal.cn: nerve 作动词是名词被派去干活：to nerve oneself 就是聚起那股绷紧的力量，在行动前稳住它。

abstract.en: A word for a physical cord becomes a word for moral steadiness, because courage feels like something pulled tight in the chest.
abstract.cn: 一个指身体细索的词变成了指精神稳定的词，因为勇气感觉像胸腔里有什么被拉紧了。

abstract.en: The distance from courage to cheek is short: both are strength that refuses to be held back by other people's expectations.
abstract.cn: 从勇气到厚脸皮只隔一小步：两者都是不肯被旁人期待挡回去的力量。

abstract.en: Nerve can be a fibre, a feeling, a virtue, an insult and an action, which shows how far one bodily image can travel.
abstract.cn: nerve 可以是纤维、感觉、美德、骂人的话，也可以是一个动作，可见一个身体意象能走多远。

examples.en: A damaged nerve can take months to heal.
examples.cn: 受损的神经可能需要几个月才能愈合。

examples.en: She lost her nerve and stepped back from the edge.
examples.cn: 她失去了勇气，从边缘退了回来。

examples.en: He nerved himself to open the letter.
examples.cn: 他鼓起勇气拆开了那封信。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢夫」——神经绷得像一根细线，人也跟着紧张起来；nerve 就是神经、勇气。

root: 拉丁语 nervus（筋、肌腱、神经）经古法语 nerf 进入英语；一般认为与希腊语 neuron（筋、神经）同源，同族词有 nervous、nervously、enervate 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a taut cord in the body; anatomy supplies the fibre, and the tautness supplies courage, cheek, tension and the act of steeling oneself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是身体里一根绷紧的索；解剖提供纤维义，绷紧感则提供勇气、厚脸皮、紧张不安与鼓劲这几个义项。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thin white cord running from the spine to a fingertip, carrying a small electric pulse when touched.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根细白索从脊柱伸到指尖，被触碰时传过一小阵电流。

branches.en: a nerve cell seen under a microscope
branches.cn: 显微镜下的一枚神经细胞

branches.en: a dentist numbing one side of the jaw

intro.en: The word is a Latin noun for sinew, its adjective of strength, the French form that carried it, and the English words that grew from the same stem.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语表示「筋」的名词、表示强壮的形容词、承载它的法语形式，以及同一词干上的英语词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied the noun for sinew and the adjective for strength, and French passed the noun to English before the metaphor of courage developed.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「筋」的名词与「强壮」的形容词，法语把名词传给英语，之后才发展出勇气的比喻。

definition_en: anxious and easily worried; relating to the nerves of the body; highly strung and quick to react
core_image: 考场门口，一个女生反复整理袖口，眼睛盯着紧闭的门
scene: 考前的走廊里，一个女生站在门口，手指一遍遍捏着袖口，眼睛盯着紧闭的教室门。She felt nervous before the oral exam, so she kept checking her notes.
sceneCN: 这里是「紧张的、焦虑的」（第 1 个义项：面对考验时心里不安）；句意为口试之前她感到紧张，所以不停地看笔记。图中可辨识物件：走廊、袖口、教室门。

senses.title: Anxious and unable to relax
senses.definition: worried and unable to relax because something important or uncertain is about to happen
senses.definitionCN: 因为重要或不确定的事即将发生而担心、无法放松
senses.example: She felt nervous before the oral exam, so she kept checking her notes.
senses.exampleCN: 口试之前她感到紧张，所以不停地看笔记。
senses.why: The word born from sinews came to describe a body whose threads are pulled tight; English then read that tightness as worry, so a physical tension became the ordinary word for anxiety.
senses.whyCN: 这个从「筋」生出的词，后来形容身体里一根根线被拉紧的状态；英语又把这种紧绷读成担忧，于是身体的紧张成了日常表示焦虑的词。

senses.title: Relating to the nerves of the body
senses.definition: connected with the fibres and tissue that carry signals in the body
senses.definitionCN: 与体内传递信号的纤维和组织有关的
senses.example: Nervous tissue carries signals from the skin to the brain.
senses.exampleCN: 神经组织把信号从皮肤传到大脑。
senses.why: This sense is the oldest technical one, because the adjective was formed directly from the noun for a bodily cord; anatomy never lost the word, even after everyday speech took it over for worry.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项是最早的技术义，因为形容词直接由表示身体细索的名词构成；即使日常口语把这个词拿去表示担忧，解剖学也从未丢掉它。

senses.title: Highly strung and quick to react
senses.definition: easily excited or upset, reacting strongly to small things
senses.definitionCN: 容易兴奋或不安，对小事反应强烈
senses.example: The nervous dog hid under the table when the doorbell rang.
senses.exampleCN: 门铃一响，那只见人易惊的狗就躲到了桌子底下。
senses.why: An animal with fine, quick reactions is described as loosely strung rather than steady, so the same anatomical word moved from the wiring of the body to the temperament of a person or animal.
senses.whyCN: 反应细密而迅捷的动物，被形容为绳弦调得过松、不够稳当；于是同一个解剖词从身体的线路上，移到了人或动物的性情上。

intro.en: Nervous is the Latin adjective of sinew, which English first used for strong bodies and later for bodies whose nerves react too quickly.
intro.cn: nervous 是拉丁语中表示「筋」的形容词，英语先用它形容强壮的身体，后来才用它形容神经反应过快的人。

items.en: Nervus meant sinew, tendon or cord, the visible thread running through flesh and bone.
items.cn: nervus 意为筋、肌腱或细索，也就是穿过血肉与骨骼的可见细线。

items.en: Nervosus meant full of sinew, strong and vigorous, and it is the direct source of the English adjective.
items.cn: nervosus 意为多筋的、强壮的、有力的，是英语这个形容词的直接来源。

items.en: Old French nerveux kept the sense of strong and sinewy and passed the adjective into English with its spelling reshaped.
items.cn: 古法语 nerveux 保留「强壮、多筋」的意思，把形容词传入英语，拼写也做了改写。

items.en: English first praised nervous strength in bodies and writing; by the eighteenth century the word had moved to people whose nerves reacted too sharply.
items.cn: 英语最初用 nervous 称赞身体与文章中的强劲；到十八世纪，这个词转向形容神经反应过于敏锐的人。

items.en: Modern English keeps the anatomical sense beside the everyday one of worry, and applies the word to people, animals and situations alike.
items.cn: 现代英语把解剖义与日常的担忧义并排保留，并且把人、动物与处境都用这个词来形容。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the noun, adverb, abstract noun and informal adjective of the same family; the near-meaning group holds words for tension and low-level fear.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的名称、副词、抽象名词与口语形容词；近义组收表示紧绷与轻微恐惧的词。

entries.definition: The fibre itself, and also courage or boldness, the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 纤维本身，也指勇气或放肆，是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: In an anxious manner, made by adding -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以焦虑的方式；加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The state of being anxious, made with -ness.
entries.definitionCN: 焦虑的状态；由 -ness 构成。

entries.definition: Anxious in British use, but bold in American use, made with -y.
entries.definitionCN: 英式指紧张不安，美式却指有胆量；由 -y 构成。

entries.definition: Worried about something uncertain, often with a sense of dread.
entries.definitionCN: 对不确定之事担忧，常带一点恐惧。

entries.definition: Tight and strained, used of muscles, situations and people alike.
entries.definitionCN: 绷紧、吃力的，可用于肌肉、局面与人。

entries.definition: Unable to keep still because of nerves, especially before an event.
entries.definitionCN: 因紧张而静不下来，尤指事情发生之前。

entries.definition: Slightly worried or uncomfortable, milder than nervous.
entries.definitionCN: 略有担忧或不舒服，语气比 nervous 轻。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of sinew, and its senses keep the same taut thread, read first as strength, then as sensitivity, then as worry.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「筋」的形容词，各义项保留同一根绷紧的线，先读作力量，再读作敏感，最后读作担忧。

normal.en: Nervous is built on nerve with the Latin ending -ous, so its literal shape is full of sinew.
normal.cn: nervous 由 nerve 加拉丁词尾 -ous 构成，字面形状就是「充满筋腱」。

normal.en: That literal sense praised strength, which is why older writing can call a vigorous style nervous.
normal.cn: 这个字面义曾用来称赞力量，所以较旧的文字会用 nervous 形容有劲的文风。

normal.en: The modern sense reversed the praise: a body whose nerves are too responsive is easily unsettled.
normal.cn: 现代义把这种称赞反了过来：神经反应过于灵敏的身体容易受扰。

normal.en: The anatomical sense survives in fixed phrases such as nervous system and nervous tissue.
normal.cn: 解剖义留在 nervous system、nervous tissue 这类固定搭配里。

normal.en: Nervously and nervousness simply add the manner and the state to the same adjective, so the family grows without a new root.
normal.cn: nervously 与 nervousness 只是给同一形容词加上方式与状态，词族因此不必另换词根。

abstract.en: A word for strong sinew becomes a word for fragile nerves, because the same thread can be praised as taut or blamed as over-sensitive.
abstract.cn: 一个指强健筋腱的词变成了指脆弱神经的词，因为同一根线既可以被赞为绷得紧，也可以被怪为过于敏感。

abstract.en: Standing before a closed door is the perfect picture of nervousness: the body is ready before it knows what will happen.
abstract.cn: 站在一扇关着的门前，是紧张最贴切的画面：身体在知道会发生什么之前就已经准备好了。

abstract.en: English lets one adjective cover the wiring of the body and the worry of the mind, which is how close the two have always been.
abstract.cn: 英语让一个形容词同时覆盖身体的线路与心里的担忧，可见这两者从来就很近。

examples.en: She gets nervous whenever she speaks in public.
examples.cn: 她每次当众讲话都会紧张。

examples.en: The nervous system controls how the body reacts.
examples.cn: 神经系统控制身体如何反应。

examples.en: He gave a nervous laugh and looked away.
examples.cn: 他局促地笑了一声，把目光移开。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一根绷紧的索；由此长出解剖义、反应迅捷的性情，以及日常的焦虑感。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of

definition_zh: 紧张地；不安地；局促地；焦躁地
definition_en: in an anxious or worried way; with shy awkwardness; in a restless, fidgety manner
core_image: 长椅上的一支笔在指间转个不停，桌角的纸被折了又展平
scene: 面试室外的长椅上，年轻人低头坐着，一支笔在指间转个不停。He tapped his foot nervously while waiting for his name to be called.
sceneCN: 这里是「紧张不安地」（第 1 个义项：心里发紧、动作无法放松）；句意为等叫名字的时候，他紧张地一直跺脚。图中可辨识物件：长椅、转动的笔、折过的纸角。

pos.zh: 紧张地；不安地；局促地；焦躁地

derivatives.zh: nervously 的词根，义为「紧张的；神经的」

nervous 的来源词，义为「神经；勇气」

senses.title: In an anxious, worried manner
senses.definition: in a way that shows worry and an inability to relax
senses.definitionCN: 以显出担忧、无法放松的方式
senses.example: He tapped his foot nervously while waiting for his name to be called.
senses.exampleCN: 等叫名字的时候，他紧张地一直跺脚。
senses.why: The ending -ly turns the adjective of taut nerves into the manner of an action, so nervously always describes a body that cannot settle while it waits.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -ly 把表示「神经绷紧」的形容词变成动作的方式，所以 nervously 描述的总是等待时无法安顿下来的身体。

senses.title: With shy awkwardness
senses.definition: in a shy, awkward way that shows a person is unsure what to do or say
senses.definitionCN: 以害羞、笨拙的方式，显出不确定该做什么或说什么
senses.example: She laughed nervously and changed the subject.
senses.exampleCN: 她局促地笑了笑，把话题岔开。
senses.why: Social pressure produces the same tightness as danger does, and the small, mismatched movements it causes are read by others as awkwardness, so the adverb also names the manner of someone out of place.
senses.whyCN: 社交压力造成的紧绷与危险带来的紧绷相同，由此产生的小而失当的动作在旁人眼里就是局促，所以这个副词也命名「格格不入」时的举止。

senses.title: In a restless, fidgety manner
senses.definition: in a way that shows repeated small movements caused by tension
senses.definitionCN: 以因紧张而反复做出小动作的方式
senses.example: The boy shifted nervously in his chair all through the film.
senses.exampleCN: 整场电影里，那个男孩都在椅子上焦躁地挪来挪去。
senses.why: Restlessness is tension expressed through repetition, and the adverb reports the rhythm of those tiny movements rather than the feeling behind them.
senses.whyCN: 坐立不安是把紧张通过重复动作表达出来，这个副词报告的是那些细微动作的节奏，而不是背后的感受。

intro.en: Nervously is the adjective of taut nerves fitted with the English manner ending, so its history is the history of nervous plus -ly.
intro.cn: nervously 是表示「神经绷紧」的形容词配上英语方式词尾，它的历史就是 nervous 加 -ly 的历史。

items.en: Nervus meant sinew or tendon, the cord that keeps a body taut and ready.
items.cn: nervus 意为筋或肌腱，是让身体绷紧、随时待命的索。

items.en: Nervosus meant full of sinew and therefore strong, and it gave English the adjective nervous.
items.cn: nervosus 意为多筋的、因而强壮的，它给英语提供了形容词 nervous。

items.en: English nervous moved from praising strength to naming quick reactions and then everyday worry.
items.cn: 英语的 nervous 从称赞力量，转到指反应迅捷，再转到日常的担忧。

items.en: The Old English ending -lice became -ly, turning adjectives of state into adverbs of how an action is carried out.
items.cn: 古英语词尾 -lice 变成 -ly，把表示状态的形容词变成说明动作如何进行的方式副词。

items.en: Modern English uses nervously for waiting, laughing, glancing and shifting, keeping one adverb for every visible form of tension.
items.cn: 现代英语把 nervously 用于等待、发笑、瞥视与挪动，各种看得见的紧张都用同一个副词。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adjective, the abstract noun and the root noun of the same family; the near-meaning group holds other adverbs of fear and strain.
note.cn: 形近组收同一词族的形容词、抽象名词与词根名词；近义组收其他表示恐惧与紧绷的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective of anxiety and of the nerves themselves.
entries.definitionCN: 表示焦虑以及神经本身的形容词。

entries.definition: The state that nervously describes when it appears in an action.
entries.definitionCN: nervously 所描述的那种状态本身。

entries.definition: The fibre, or the courage and boldness that share its name.
entries.definitionCN: 纤维，或与之同名的勇气与放肆。

entries.definition: Anxious in British English, bold in American English.
entries.definitionCN: 英式英语指紧张，美式英语指有胆量。

entries.definition: In a worried way, often with a sense of waiting for bad news.
entries.definitionCN: 以担忧的方式，常带等待坏消息的意味。

entries.definition: With the body or atmosphere drawn tight, stressing strain rather than fear.
entries.definitionCN: 身体或气氛绷得很紧，强调吃力而非害怕。

entries.definition: In a mildly worried or uncomfortable way, softer than nervously.
entries.definitionCN: 以略有担忧或不适的方式，语气比 nervously 轻。

entries.definition: In a shy, fearful way, stressing lack of confidence rather than tension.
entries.definitionCN: 以羞怯、害怕的方式，强调缺乏自信而非紧绷。

normalIntro.en: The word is nervous with the manner ending -ly, so it reports how tension shows itself in small actions.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 nervous 加方式词尾 -ly，所以它报告的是紧张如何通过细小动作显出来。

normal.en: Nervous is the adjective and nervously the adverb: a nervous wait, but he waited nervously.
normal.cn: nervous 是形容词，nervously 是副词：说 a nervous wait，但说 he waited nervously。

normal.en: The ending -ly goes back to Old English -lice and means in the manner of, so nervously names the way, not the feeling.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 可追到古英语 -lice，意为「以……的方式」，所以 nervously 命名的是方式，而不是感受。

normal.en: Nervously keeps the tight-thread picture of nerve, which is why it suits tapping feet and turning pens.
normal.cn: nervously 保留了 nerve 那根绷紧细线的画面，所以它很适合形容跺脚与转笔。

normal.en: Laughing nervously and smiling nervously both show tension leaking into the face when words fail.
normal.cn: laugh nervously 与 smile nervously 都表现话说不下去时，紧张从脸上漏出来。

normal.en: In writing, nervously often marks a character who is trying too hard to seem calm.
normal.cn: 在写作里，nervously 常用来标记一个拼命想显得镇定的人物。

abstract.en: An adverb of anxiety is really a report on the body's small leaks: the foot, the pen and the folded paper corner.
abstract.cn: 一个表示焦虑的副词，其实是在报告身体漏出来的小动作：脚、笔与折起的纸角。

abstract.en: Waiting is where nervously does its clearest work, because nothing can be done and the body keeps moving anyway.
abstract.cn: 等待是 nervously 最能说明自己的场合，因为什么也做不了，身体却仍在动。

abstract.en: Nervously is nervous seen from the side of the action, which is why it always answers the question of how.
abstract.cn: nervously 是从动作那一侧看到的 nervous，所以它回答的总是「怎么做」。

examples.en: She waited nervously outside the office.
examples.cn: 她在办公室外紧张地等着。

examples.en: He smiled nervously and said nothing.
examples.cn: 他局促地笑了笑，什么也没说。

examples.en: The child clung nervously to his mother's hand.
examples.cn: 那孩子紧张地抓着母亲的手。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢维丝利」——神经绷成一根细丝，动作就变得局促；nervously 就是紧张地。

root: 由 nervous（紧张的，源自拉丁语 nervus「筋」加 -ous）加副词词尾 -ly 构成；本义「以神经紧绷的方式」，引申为紧张地、局促地、焦躁地。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the visible manner of tension; waiting, laughing and shifting are three places where that manner shows itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是紧张看得见的举止；等待、发笑与挪动，是这种举止显现的三个场合。

sceneCN: 这里 nest 指「鸟巢、窝」（第 1 个义项：动物为产卵育雏而筑的结构）；句意为一只麻雀的巢卡在梁边，里面三枚卵还是温的；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 巢；窝；巢穴；一窝（卵或雏）
筑巢；巢居；嵌套；层层套放

derivatives.zh: 筑巢；筑巢期的
筑巢的鸟；营巢者
巢中雏鸟
嵌套的
巢箱

senses.title: A structure built to hold eggs
senses.titleCN: 为盛放卵而筑成的结构
senses.definition: a structure of twigs, mud, grass or other material in which a bird lays and incubates eggs
senses.definitionCN: 用树枝、泥、草等材料筑成、鸟在其中产卵与孵卵的结构
senses.example: A sparrow's nest sat wedged against the beam.
senses.exampleCN: 一只麻雀的巢卡在梁边。
senses.why: the core sense is simply the object, because everything else the word names is derived from this built container.
senses.whyCN: 核心义就是这件物体，因为这个词命名的其它一切都是由这个容器引申出来的。

senses.title: The home of a whole brood
senses.definition: the place where a brood is reared, viewed as the young family's home
senses.definitionCN: 一窝雏被养育之处，被看作这个幼小家庭的家
senses.example: The whole nest begged whenever the adult landed.
senses.exampleCN: 成鸟一落下，整窝雏鸟都乞食。
senses.why: the container and its occupants merge, so nest may name the family inside as much as the structure.
senses.whyCN: 容器与其居住者合并，因此 nest 既可指结构，也可指里面的全家。

senses.title: A clutch counted as one unit
senses.definition: the set of eggs laid in one nest and incubated together
senses.definitionCN: 在同一巢中产出并一起孵化的一组卵
senses.example: Rangers recorded a nest of four eggs under the lamp.
senses.exampleCN: 巡护员在灯下记录到一窝四枚卵。
senses.why: counting by nests is convenient because the nest defines the set, so the container becomes the unit of number.
senses.whyCN: 以巢计数很方便，因为巢定义了这一组，容器于是成了计数单位。

senses.title: A hollow made by another animal
senses.titleCN: 由其它动物挖出的巢穴
senses.definition: a burrow, hole or cavity used by an insect, mammal or fish for young
senses.definitionCN: 昆虫、哺乳动物或鱼为育幼而使用的洞、穴或腔
senses.example: Wasps build a paper nest under the roof tiles.
senses.exampleCN: 黄蜂在屋瓦下筑成纸质的巢。
senses.why: once the word is applied beyond birds, the structure stops being woven and becomes any prepared cavity.
senses.whyCN: 一旦越出鸟类，这个结构就不再是编织的，而成为任何备好的腔室。

senses.title: To build and occupy a nest
senses.definition: to build a nest and use it for breeding
senses.definitionCN: 建造巢并将其用于繁殖
senses.example: Swallows nest every year in the same corner of the barn.
senses.exampleCN: 燕子每年都在谷仓同一个角落筑巢。
senses.why: the verb is simply the noun turned into an action, so it means to do what the noun names.
senses.whyCN: 动词就是名词转为动作，意为做出名词所指的那件事。

senses.title: To place one thing inside another
senses.titleCN: 把一物套进另一物内部
senses.definition: to fit objects or structures one inside another, as boxes or data tables
senses.definitionCN: 把物件或结构放进彼此内部，如盒子或数据表
senses.example: Nest the smaller boxes inside the larger crate.
senses.exampleCN: 把小盒子套进大板条箱里。
senses.why: the technical sense generalizes the shape of the bird's cup: something held within something else.
senses.whyCN: 技术义把鸟巢的形状一般化：一物被另一物容纳在其中。

senses.title: A graduated set that fits inside itself
senses.titleCN: 可以逐层套放的一组器物
senses.definition: a set of similar objects of decreasing size that store one inside another, as a nest of tables
senses.definitionCN: 一组大小递减、可以互相套放的同类物件，如套几
senses.example: The nest of tables slotted under the largest one.
senses.exampleCN: 套几收进最大的那张下面。
senses.why: the noun is applied to objects that imitate the containment of a nest, so the name follows the shape rather than the bird.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词被用于模仿「巢的容纳关系」的物件，因此名称追随形状而非鸟。

senses.title: A den of troublesome people or things
senses.titleCN: 滋生麻烦的人或事物之处
senses.definition: a place or group seen as a breeding ground for something harmful, as in a nest of thieves
senses.definitionCN: 被视为有害之物滋生地的场所或群体，如贼窝
senses.example: The yard had become a nest of infection after the flood.
senses.exampleCN: 洪水之后这个院子成了感染滋生地。
senses.why: the metaphor keeps only the idea of a sheltered place where something grows, and that something is no longer young.
senses.whyCN: 比喻只保留「有遮蔽之处、某种东西在其中生长」的意思，而生长之物已不再是幼鸟。

intro.en: Nest is an Old English word, nest, with the same form in several old Germanic languages; its relation to Latin nidus is debated rather than settled.
intro.cn: nest 是古英语词 nest，在数种古老日耳曼语中形式相同；它与拉丁 nidus 的关系属争议，未有定论。

items.en: Old English nest named both the structure and the brood in it, and the word has kept that double reach.
items.cn: 古英语 nest 既指结构，也指其中的一窝，这双重范围一直保留。

items.en: Old Norse nest, Old High German nest and Middle Dutch nest show a common Germanic stock, so Latin borrowing is unlikely.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 nest、古高地德语 nest、中古荷兰语 nest 表明共同的日耳曼来源，因此不太可能是拉丁借词。

items.en: Latin nidus 'nest' looks similar and means the same, but most handbooks treat the resemblance as parallel; a shared Indo-European source is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 拉丁 nidus「巢」形似义同，但多数辞书把这种相似视为平行；共有印欧来源属重构形式。

items.en: Source uncertain (root): the pre-Germanic shape of nest is unresolved; the root commonly printed for it is reconstructed, not attested.
items.cn: 来源不确定（词根）：nest 在日耳曼语之前的形式无定论；常印出的词根是重构形式，并非有证材料。

items.en: The verb nest appeared later, formed directly from the noun, and was extended to any placing of one thing inside another.
items.cn: 动词 nest 出现较晚，直接由名词构成，并被扩展到任何把一物放进另一物的动作。

items.en: Phrases such as empty nest and nest egg carried the word into family life and household finance.
items.cn: empty nest、nest egg 等短语把这个词带进家庭生活与家庭理财。

note.en: Group one separates the near-synonyms for animal homes; group two separates the words built on nest itself.
note.cn: 第一组区分表示动物居所近义词；第二组区分由 nest 本身构成的词。

entries.definition: The -ing form names the building and sitting; the bare nest names the object.
entries.definitionCN: -ing 形式指建与伏的行为；原形 nest 指物件。

entries.definition: A nestling is a chick too young to leave; it is the content of the nest, not the nest.
entries.definitionCN: nestling 是尚不能离巢的雏鸟，是巢中之物，而非巢。

entries.definition: A nester is the bird regarded as the one that nests, marked by -er.
entries.definitionCN: nester 是把鸟看作筑巢者，由 -er 标记。

entries.definition: Nested describes something already placed inside another; it is a state, not a place.
entries.definitionCN: nested 描述已被放进另一物之中的状态，是状态而非地点。

entries.definition: A burrow is dug into earth or sand; a nest may be built on a branch or in a hole.
entries.definitionCN: burrow 掘入土或沙；巢可能筑在枝上或洞里。

entries.definition: A den is a mammal's shelter, often a cave or hollow, and usually not built from gathered material.
entries.definitionCN: den 是哺乳动物的居所，常为洞穴，通常不由采集材料筑成。

entries.definition: A lair is where a wild animal rests, especially a predator; it carries no idea of eggs.
entries.definitionCN: lair 是野兽尤其捕食者歇息之处，不含产卵之意。

entries.definition: A hive is the home of a bee colony, a special case of an insect nest with a fixed architecture.
entries.definitionCN: hive 是蜂群的家，是昆虫巢的一种特例，结构固定。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real Germanic relatives, real compounds and real idioms.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的日耳曼同族词、真实复合词与真实习语。

normal.en: The Germanic relatives are Old Norse nest and Old High German nest, not Latin words.
normal.cn: 日耳曼同族词是古诺斯语 nest 与古高地德语 nest，而非拉丁词。

normal.en: The family runs nest, nesting, nester, nestling, nested, nest box.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 nest、nesting、nester、nestling、nested、nest box。

normal.en: Fixed phrases: build a nest, leave the nest, nest of eggs.
normal.cn: 固定搭配：筑巢、离巢、一窝蛋。

normal.en: The idioms empty nest and nest egg show the word applied to family and savings.
normal.cn: 习语 empty nest 与 nest egg 显示这个词被用于家庭与储蓄。

normal.en: In computing, nest means to place one structure inside another.
normal.cn: 在计算机中，nest 指把一种结构放进另一种。

abstract.en: Picture a cup so exactly shaped that the sitter's body closes its opening.
abstract.cn: 想象一只碗形制精准，伏者的身体正好封住开口。

abstract.en: Picture a house whose walls keep growing back after each departure.
abstract.cn: 想象一座屋子，每次有人离开后墙壁又重新长回。

abstract.en: Picture a set of bowls where the smallest is invisible until lifted out.
abstract.cn: 想象一套碗，最小的一只不被提起就看不见。

examples.en: The nest was rebuilt on the same branch after the storm.
examples.cn: 风暴过后，巢又在同一根枝上重建。

examples.en: She found an old nest in the rafters, empty and crumbling.
examples.cn: 她在椽子上发现一只空了的旧巢，正在崩解。

examples.en: Programmers nest these records inside a parent object.
examples.cn: 程序员把这些记录嵌进一个父对象里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「nest（巢）」——树枝围成碗，卵卧其中 → 巢、窝；动作义为筑巢、套住

root: 古英语 nest「巢；一窝」，与古诺斯语、古高地德语、中古荷兰语 nest 同出日耳曼共有词；与拉丁 nidus「巢」形似义同，通常视为平行构词，共有印欧来源仅为重构形式，日耳曼以前词根来源不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow one shape: a built cup holds something precious, and the word then names the occupants, the count, a prepared cavity, a den of trouble, the act of building, any placing of one thing inside another, and finally a set of objects made to slot together.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿一个形状展开：一只编成的碗托住贵重之物，词语随后指其居住者、计数单位、备好的腔室、滋生麻烦的窝、建造动作、任何把一物放进另一物的动作，最后指一组可以互相套放的器物。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a cup woven at the branch fork, its inner walls smoothed by the body inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：枝杈分叉处编成的碗，内壁被其中的身体压得光滑。

branches.en: CUP AND FAMILY: the container and the family in it are named by the same word.
branches.cn: 碗与家庭：容器与其中的家庭由同一个词命名。

branches.en: COUNTED SET: the nest defines the clutch, so the container becomes the unit.
branches.cn: 可数的组：巢定义了这一窝，容器于是成了单位。

branches.en: A SHELTERED PLACE: any animal's cavity, and a den where trouble breeds.
branches.cn: 有遮蔽之处：任何动物的腔室，以及滋生麻烦的窝。

branches.en: DOING THE NOUN: the verb is the noun turned into an act.
branches.cn: 做名词所指的事：动词就是名词转为动作。

branches.en: SHAPE EXPORTED: a rule for holding one thing inside another, and objects made to nest.
branches.cn: 形状外输：一条「一物容另一物」的规则，以及照此造出的套叠器物。

intro.en: Nest is a bare Germanic root that takes English suffixes and compounds; it has no Latin prefix structure.
intro.cn: nest 是裸露的日耳曼词根，只接英语后缀与复合成分，没有拉丁前缀结构。

latinIntro.en: Nest itself has no Latin element; the Latin entries are the learned equivalents English borrowed separately for the same content.
latinIntro.cn: nest 本身不含拉丁成分；下列拉丁条目是英语为同一内容另行借入的学术词。

items.example: They used the bonus as a nest egg.
items.exampleCN: 他们把奖金当作储备金。

items.meaning: a home after the children leave
items.example: The empty nest felt too quiet.

items.exampleCN: 志愿者挂上了四十只巢箱。

items.example: The ruling stirred a hornet's nest.

definition_zh: 网；网状物；网络；净的；净赚；用网捕
definition_en: a material woven from threads with holes between them; the internet; remaining after all deductions; to catch or gain as a clear amount
core_image: 河湾浅水处张着一张旧渔网，网眼一格一格，兜住几条银色的鱼
scene: 天刚亮，河湾的浅水处张着一张旧渔网，网脚用石块压住。A fishing net hung across the narrow channel, and the water flowed through it.
sceneCN: 这里是「网」（第 1 个义项：用线编成、带网眼用来兜住东西的器物）；句意为一张渔网横挂在狭窄的水道上，水从网眼流过去。图中可辨识物件：河湾、渔网、压网的石块、银色的鱼。

pos.zh: 网；网状物；网络
净的；扣除后的
用网捕；净赚

derivatives.zh: 由 net 加 -ing 构成，义为「网；网材料」
由 net 与 work 复合而成，义为「网络；网状系统」
由 net 加 -ed 构成，义为「用网制成的；网状的」

senses.title: A woven mesh for catching or holding things
senses.definition: a material made of threads woven with gaps between them, used to catch fish, carry goods or stop things from falling
senses.definitionCN: 用线编成、留有网眼的材料，用来捕鱼、装货或防止东西坠落
senses.example: A fishing net hung across the narrow channel, and the water flowed through it.
senses.exampleCN: 一张渔网横挂在狭窄的水道上，水从网眼流过去。
senses.why: Old English nett named a woven trap of cords with deliberate gaps, and the gap matters as much as the cord: water passes through while fish are held back.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 nett 指用绳线编成、特意留出缺口的捕捉器，缺口与绳线同样重要：水能穿过，鱼却被拦住。

senses.title: The internet, especially as a place people enter
senses.definition: the worldwide computer network, used informally as a place people visit for information or contact
senses.definitionCN: 全球计算机网络，口语中当作人们去获取信息或联络的场所
senses.example: She spends an hour on the net every morning before work.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上上班前都要在网络上看一个小时。
senses.why: A mesh joins many separate points without needing one single path, which is exactly how a computer network links machines, so the old word for a woven trap became the name of a system with no centre.
senses.whyCN: 网把许多分散的点连起来，不需要唯一的一条路径，计算机网络连接机器正是这样；于是那个古老的编织捕捉器之名，成了一个没有中心的系统的名称。

senses.title: Remaining after all deductions
senses.definition: left over after costs, taxes or other amounts have been taken away
senses.definitionCN: 扣去成本、税项或其他数额之后剩下的
senses.example: The company reported a net profit of two million pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 公司公布了二百万英镑的净利润。
senses.why: This adjective is a different word from the mesh: French net meant clean and clear, and a clear amount is one with every deduction washed out of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词与「网」是不同的词：法语 net 意为干净、清楚，而「干净」的数额就是把每一项扣除都洗掉之后剩下的数。

senses.title: To catch in a net
senses.definition: to catch a fish, bird or ball in a net
senses.definitionCN: 用网兜住鱼、鸟或球
senses.example: They netted three fish before the tide turned.
senses.exampleCN: 潮水转向之前，他们用网捕到了三条鱼。
senses.why: The noun turned into a verb without adding a syllable, and the action is simply doing what the object was made for; netting a ball is the goalkeeper using the mesh as intended.
senses.whyCN: 名词不添一个音节就变成动词，动作不过是让器物做它本来被造出来要做的事；门将把球收进网里，就是按设计使用那张网。

senses.title: To gain as a clear amount
senses.definition: to earn or obtain an amount after everything else has been taken away
senses.definitionCN: 扣去其他一切之后赚到或得到某个数额
senses.example: The sale netted the family enough to repair the roof.
senses.exampleCN: 这笔买卖让这家人净赚了足够修屋顶的钱。
senses.why: Once net names the clean remainder, the verb can name the act of arriving at it, so money, points and results are all said to be netted when nothing is given back.
senses.whyCN: 一旦 net 指「干净的剩余」，动词就能指得到这个剩余的动作；于是钱、分数与结果在无须退还时都可以说被 netted。

intro.en: Net joins two stories: a Germanic word for a woven mesh and a French word for a clean remainder that came from Latin brightness, and English wrote both with the same three letters.
intro.cn: net 合并了两个来历：一个指编织网眼的日耳曼词，和一个经法语、来自拉丁语「光亮」的「干净剩余」；英语把两者写成了同样的三个字母。

items.en: Nett was the ordinary word for a mesh of cords used in hunting and fishing, and it also named cloth woven in the same way.
items.cn: nett 是狩猎与捕鱼所用绳网的通称，也指按同样方式织成的布。

items.en: The reconstructed Germanic form natja- stands behind nett and its cousins in the other Germanic languages.
items.cn: 重构的日耳曼语形式 natja- 位于 nett 及其他日耳曼语同族词的背后。

items.en: A second source reached English through French: Latin nitidus meant clean and bright, and Old French net meant clear and unspoiled.
items.cn: 第二个来源经法语进入英语：拉丁语 nitidus 意为干净、光亮，古法语 net 意为清楚、未受污损。

items.en: Middle English kept net for the mesh and also used net for a clear sum of money; the two words looked and were written alike, so they merged.
items.cn: 中古英语用 net 指网，也用 net 指清楚的金额；两个词形与拼写相同，于是合并了。

items.en: Modern English keeps both strands, adds the internet sense, and lets the adjective and verb carry the idea of a clean remainder.
items.cn: 现代英语保留两支来历，添上互联网义，并让形容词与动词承担「干净剩余」的意思。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the woven material, the compound built on net, and the French relative for a clean amount; the near-meaning group holds other words for meshes and for the opposite of net.
note.cn: 形近组收编织材料、建在 net 上的复合词，以及表示「干净数额」的法语亲缘词；近义组收其他表示网状物的词，以及 net 的反义词。

entries.definition: Fabric or mesh made of net, also the act of using one.
entries.definitionCN: 用网做成的布料或网，也指用网的动作。

entries.definition: A system of connected people or machines, built from net and work.
entries.definitionCN: 由 net 与 work 构成，指相互连接的人或机器的系统。

entries.definition: Tidy and clean; the adjective shares the French source of the clean-amount sense, though it looks like a short form of net.
entries.definitionCN: 整洁干净的；与「干净数额」义共享法语来源，外形却像 net 的短形式。

entries.definition: The open weave of a net, or any material with regular gaps.
entries.definitionCN: 网的编织结构，或任何带规则网眼的材料。

entries.definition: A network of fine threads, especially one spun by a spider.
entries.definitionCN: 细丝构成的网，尤指蜘蛛结的网。

entries.definition: A frame of crossed strips with regular spaces, closer to a structure than a trap.
entries.definitionCN: 交叉条板构成、留有规则空隙的框架，更接近结构而非捕捉器。

entries.definition: Total, before any deductions, the direct opposite of net in accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 未扣除任何项的总额，在账目中是 net 的直接反义。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Germanic mesh on one side and a French clean remainder on the other, and its senses divide neatly along that old seam.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词一面是日耳曼语的网，另一面是法语的「干净剩余」，各义项正好沿着这条古老的接缝分开。

normal.en: Old English nett meant a woven mesh with gaps, and the gaps are the point: what passes through is as important as what is held.
normal.cn: 古英语 nett 指留有空隙的编织网，空隙才是关键：让什么通过，与拦住什么同样重要。

normal.en: Netting and network both grow from the mesh: one is the material, the other a system joined like a mesh.
normal.cn: netting 与 network 都从「网」长出：一个是材料，另一个是像网一样连接的系统。

normal.en: Net profit is the other word: French net meant clean, and a clean sum has had every deduction taken out.
normal.cn: net profit 用的是另一个词：法语 net 意为干净，而干净的金额已经扣除了每一项。

normal.en: Neat comes from the same French source, so neat handwriting and net profit share a picture of a clean surface.
normal.cn: neat 出自同一法语来源，所以工整的字迹与净利润共享一幅「干净表面」的画面。

normal.en: The verb netted works for both strands: fish are netted in a mesh, and a deal nets a clean profit.
normal.cn: 动词 netted 两支都管：鱼被网兜住，买卖则净得一笔干净利润。

abstract.en: A trap and an accounting term ended up as one spelling, which is why a word can hold water and money at the same time.
abstract.cn: 一个捕捉器与一个会计术语最后写成了同一个拼写，所以一个词能同时兜住水和钱。

abstract.en: The mesh teaches that connection does not need a centre, a lesson the internet inherited from a fishing tool.
abstract.cn: 网说明连接不需要中心，这是互联网从一件渔具继承来的道理。

abstract.en: What is net is what remains when everything extra has passed through, just as water passes through the mesh.
abstract.cn: 「净」的东西就是一切多余之物穿过去之后剩下的，正如水穿过网眼。

examples.en: The goalkeeper caught the ball in the net.
examples.cn: 守门员把球收进网里。

examples.en: She checks the net for the latest news.
examples.cn: 她上网查看最新消息。

examples.en: The deal netted them enough money to move house.
examples.cn: 这笔交易让他们净赚了足够搬家的钱。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内特」——网眼一格一格，兜住鱼也兜住利润；net 就是网、净的。

root: 网义来自古英语 nett（一般认为源自原始日耳曼语 natja-）；「净的」义经古法语 net 来自拉丁语 nitidus（干净的、光亮的），两个同形词在现代英语中合并。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a woven structure with gaps; the gaps catch fish, link computers, and let a clean remainder emerge after everything else passes through.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一个留有空隙的编织结构；空隙兜住鱼、连起计算机，也让其他一切穿过后留下干净的剩余。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an old fishing net stretched across shallow water, held down by stones, with silver fish caught in its open squares.
core.cn: 核心意象：浅水里张着一张旧渔网，网脚被石块压住，网眼兜着几条银色的鱼。

branches.cn: 天亮时横挂在水道上的网

branches.en: a safety net under a high wire
branches.cn: 高架钢丝下方的安全网

branches.en: an hour of news read online
branches.cn: 在网上读一小时新闻

intro.en: The word is a Germanic mesh noun, a French adjective of cleanliness, the Latin brightness behind it, and the English forms built from both strands.
intro.cn: 这个词由日耳曼语「网」名词、法语表示干净的形容词、其背后的拉丁语「光亮」，以及两支长出的英语形式共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: The mesh word is Germanic, while the sense of a clean remainder comes from Latin nitidus through French, so the two origins sit side by side inside one spelling.
latinIntro.cn: 「网」的词是日耳曼语，而「干净剩余」义经法语来自拉丁语 nitidus，两个来源并排躺在一个拼写里。

senses.title: A mesh of connected lines: netting
senses.titleCN: 连成一片的网线：网状织物
senses.definition: a structure of cords or threads crossed and knotted so that every part is linked to the rest
senses.definitionCN: 由绳线交叉打结而成的结构，每一处都与其他部分相连
senses.example: A torn network of netting lay across the harbour stones.
senses.exampleCN: 一张破了的网摊在港口的石头上。
senses.why: Network began in the 1550s as net plus work, literally a net-like fabric or structure. The picture is physical: knots joined by threads.
senses.whyCN: network 在 16 世纪 50 年代由 net 加 work 构成，字面是“网一样的织物或结构”。画面是实体的：网结被网线连起来。

senses.title: An interlocking transport system
senses.definition: a system of rivers, canals, roads, or railways that cross and connect at many points
senses.definitionCN: 河流、运河、道路或铁路在许多点上交叉相连的系统
senses.example: A network of canals linked the inland farms to the port.
senses.exampleCN: 一张运河网把内陆农场与港口连了起来。
senses.why: The 1839 sense 'any complex, interlocking system' was first used of rivers, canals and railways. The mesh becomes a map of routes.
senses.whyCN: 1839 年出现的“任何复杂交织的系统”一义，最初用于河流、运河与铁路。实体的网变成了一张路线图。

senses.title: A broadcasting system of many transmitters
senses.titleCN: 由多个发射台组成的广播网
senses.definition: a group of radio or television stations that share programmes and transmit them over a wide area
senses.definitionCN: 共享节目、向广大地区播送的广播电台或电视台群体
senses.example: The radio network broadcast the speech to forty stations.
senses.exampleCN: 这家广播网把演讲播送到四十家电台。
senses.why: From 1914 the word named a broadcasting system of multiple transmitters. Signals travel from node to node, so the mesh becomes a web of stations.
senses.whyCN: 从 1914 年起，这个词指由多个发射台组成的广播系统。信号从一个节点传到另一个节点，网于是变成了一张电台之网。

senses.title: An interconnected group of people
senses.definition: a group of people who are connected through work, family, or shared interests and can help one another
senses.definitionCN: 通过工作、家庭或共同兴趣相连、能互相帮助的一群人
senses.example: Her network of former classmates helped her find work.
senses.exampleCN: 她由老同学组成的人脉网帮她找到了工作。
senses.why: The 1934 sense came from psychology: people as nodes, relationships as threads. The mesh is now social rather than physical.
senses.whyCN: 1934 年的义项来自心理学术语：人是节点，关系是网线。此时网是社会性的，而非实体的。

senses.title: A computer network: machines that talk
senses.titleCN: 计算机网络：会互相通信的机器
senses.definition: a set of computers and devices connected so that they can exchange data
senses.definitionCN: 为交换数据而连接起来的一组计算机与设备
senses.example: The lab's computers share one network and one printer.
senses.exampleCN: 实验室的计算机共用一个网络和一台打印机。
senses.why: When computers became nodes, the old mesh needed no new shape: each machine is a knot, each cable a thread. The word kept its picture and changed its material.
senses.whyCN: 当计算机成为节点时，这张网不需要新形状：每台机器是一个结，每根线缆是一根网线。词保留了画面，只换了材料。

senses.title: A utility grid: power and telephone lines
senses.titleCN: 公用事业网：电力与电话线路
senses.definition: the connected system of cables, pipes, or lines that carries power, water, or telephone signals
senses.definitionCN: 输送电力、水或电话信号的互联电缆、管道或线路系统
senses.example: The power network failed during the storm.
senses.exampleCN: 暴风雨期间电网瘫痪了。
senses.why: A grid is a mesh laid over a region. Power lines join substations as knots join threads, so network names any utility system with that shape.
senses.whyCN: 电网是铺在一片区域上的网。电线把变电站连起来，正如网线把网结连起来，因此 network 可指任何具此形状的公用系统。

senses.title: To cover with a net
senses.definition: to cover an area or object with netting, usually for protection
senses.definitionCN: 用网覆盖一片区域或一个物体，通常是为了保护
senses.example: They networked the orchard to keep the birds off the fruit.
senses.exampleCN: 他们用网罩住果园，防止鸟啄食果实。
senses.why: The verb appeared in 1887 with the plainest sense: to put a net over something. It turns the noun's object into an action.
senses.whyCN: 动词义于 1887 年出现，意思最直白：把网盖在某物上。它把名词所指的对象变成了一个动作。

senses.title: To broadcast across a network
senses.definition: to send a programme out through several linked stations at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时通过多家相连的电台或电视台播送节目
senses.example: The show was networked across the whole country.
senses.exampleCN: 这个节目通过广播网在全国播送。
senses.why: From 1940 the verb meant to distribute a programme through a network of transmitters. The broadcast travels along every thread of the mesh.
senses.whyCN: 从 1940 年起，动词指通过发射台网络分发节目。广播沿着这张网的每一根线传出去。

senses.title: To connect computers together
senses.definition: to link computers or devices so that they can share data
senses.definitionCN: 把计算机或设备连接起来，使它们能共享数据
senses.example: Engineers networked the two sites with fibre-optic cable.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师用光纤把两个站点联网。
senses.why: The 1972 computing sense turns the noun into a task: you tie new knots into the existing mesh until the machines can reach one another.
senses.whyCN: 1972 年的计算机义把名词变成一个任务：你把新的结系进已有的网里，直到机器能彼此抵达。

senses.title: To build professional contacts
senses.definition: to meet and cultivate useful contacts, especially for work
senses.definitionCN: 结识并经营有用的人脉，尤指为工作目的
senses.example: She networks at every conference she attends.
senses.exampleCN: 她每参加一次会议就经营一次人脉。
senses.why: The 1982 sense applies the verb to people: each new acquaintance is a knot added to a personal mesh. Nothing physical remains but the shape.
senses.whyCN: 1982 年的义项把动词用在人身上：每位新认识的人都是加入个人之网的一个结。实体消失了，只剩形状。

intro.en: Network is a plain English compound of net and work, first recorded in the 1550s for net-like fabric. Its modern senses are a series of metaphors laid on that mesh: transport in 1839, broadcasting in 1914, people in 1934, and finally computers.
intro.cn: network 是 net 与 work 的朴素英语复合词，16 世纪 50 年代首次记录，指网一样的织物。它的现代义项是一层层叠加在这张网上的比喻：1839 年的交通、1914 年的广播、1934 年的人群，最后是计算机。

items.en: Net is Old English net 'net, snare', a word old enough to serve as a metaphor for a moral or mental trap.
items.cn: net 是古英语 net“网、罗网”，这个词古老到可以被用作道德或心理陷阱的比喻。

items.en: Network is first recorded in the 1550s as net plus work, meaning a net-like fabric or structure.
items.cn: network 于 16 世纪 50 年代首次记录，由 net 加 work 构成，指网一样的织物或结构。

items.en: The sense 'any complex, interlocking system' appears in 1839, first applied to networks of rivers, canals and railways.
items.cn: “任何复杂交织的系统”一义出现于 1839 年，最初用于河流、运河与铁路的网络。

items.en: A network becomes a broadcasting system of multiple transmitters in 1914.
items.cn: 1914 年，network 开始指由多个发射台组成的广播系统。

items.en: The sense 'interconnected group of people' appears in 1934 as psychological jargon.
items.cn: “彼此相连的人群”一义于 1934 年出现，原为心理学术语。

items.en: The verb follows: to cover with a net in 1887, to broadcast in 1940, to link computers in 1972, and to build contacts in 1982.
items.cn: 动词随后跟进：1887 年“用网覆盖”，1940 年“通过广播网播送”，1972 年“计算机联网”，1982 年“建立人脉”。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and sound, including a phrase that sounds like network; the second group is chosen for the mesh image they share.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写与读音挑选，其中有一个听起来像 network 的短语；第二组按它们共享的网状意象挑选。

entries.definition: the total value of assets minus liabilities. The phrase sounds almost like network but belongs to finance, not to nets.
entries.definitionCN: 资产总值减去负债。这个短语听起来几乎和 network 一样，但属于财务，与网无关。

entries.definition: a small, low-cost laptop of the late 2000s. It joins net to book, not to work.
entries.definitionCN: 21 世纪末流行的小型低价笔记本电脑。它把 net 与 book 组合，而不是与 work 组合。

entries.definition: material made of net or mesh. It is the noun from net, not a form of network.
entries.definitionCN: 网材；网。它是 net 派生的名词，不是 network 的变形。

entries.definition: a mesh spun by a spider, or any complex system of linked parts. It stresses threads woven by a maker, while network stresses nodes joined together.
entries.definitionCN: 蜘蛛结的网，或任何由相连部分构成的复杂系统。它强调由造物者织出的线，而 network 强调节点之间的连接。

entries.definition: a pattern of crossing lines, especially for power or streets. It is regular and geometric, while a network can grow irregularly.
entries.definitionCN: 交叉线构成的格网，尤指电网或街道网。它是规则、几何的，而 network 可以不规则地生长。

entries.definition: a material of connected strands with open spaces between them. It names the fabric itself rather than the system it forms.
entries.definitionCN: 由相连线股构成、中间有空隙的材料。它指织物本身，而不是织物形成的系统。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: net plus work in 1550s, then the dated extensions to transport, broadcasting, people and computers.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：16 世纪 50 年代的 net 加 work，随后是有年代可查的扩展——交通、广播、人群与计算机。

normal.en: net plus work says the whole thing plainly: work made of net, a net-like fabric.
normal.cn: net 加 work 说得很直白：用网做成的制成品，即网一样的织物。

normal.en: In 1839 the mesh became a map: rivers, canals and railways crossing at many points.
normal.cn: 1839 年，这张网变成了一张地图：河流、运河与铁路在许多点上交叉。

normal.en: In 1914 the mesh became stations: many transmitters sharing one broadcast.
normal.cn: 1914 年，这张网变成了电台：多个发射台共享一次广播。

normal.en: In 1934 people became the nodes, and in 1972 computers did: the shape stayed, the material changed.
normal.cn: 1934 年人成了节点，1972 年计算机成了节点：形状没变，材料变了。

normal.en: The verbs follow the nouns: cover with a net, broadcast, connect, and build contacts.
normal.cn: 动词跟随名词：用网覆盖、播送、联网、建立人脉。

abstract.en: Picture one knot with four threads leaving it: remove the threads and it is only a knot; the connections are what make it a network.
abstract.cn: 想象一个网结向四面伸出四根线：抽掉线，它只是个结；正是连接使它成为网络。

abstract.en: The same drawing works for a map, a radio system, a group of friends, and a room of servers.
abstract.cn: 同一幅图可以画成地图、广播系统、朋友圈，也可以画成一屋子的服务器。

abstract.en: Cut one thread and the mesh still holds: a network is judged by how many routes remain, not by any single knot.
abstract.cn: 剪断一根线，网仍然撑得住：网络的价值在于还剩多少条通路，而不在任何一个结。

examples.en: A dense network of trails connects the villages along the valley.
examples.cn: 一张密集的小路网连接着山谷里的村庄。

examples.en: The company rebuilt its computer network after the outage.
examples.cn: 停电事故后，公司重建了计算机网络。

examples.en: He spent the conference networking with editors and researchers.
examples.cn: 他在会议上忙着与编辑和研究人员建立人脉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「内特网」——内里特别多网结，四面八方都连着 → network 网络、人脉

root: 由古英语 net“网、罗网”加 work“工作、制成品”复合而成，1550s 首次记录，核心是“网一样的连结结构”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of network all keep one shape: knots joined by threads. The material changes from cord to canals, transmitters, people, cables and computers, and the verb senses simply put the mesh into action.
sensesIntro.cn: network 的十个义项都保留同一个形状：网结被网线连起来。材料从绳索换成运河、发射台、人、电缆与计算机，动词义只是让这张网动起来。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fishing net spread out, every knot tied to others.
core.cn: 核心意象：一张摊开的渔网，每个网结都连着别的结。

branches.en: FROM FABRIC TO MAP: literal netting, then a system of rivers, canals and railways.
branches.cn: 从织物到地图：字面的网，然后是河流、运河与铁路构成的系统。

branches.en: FROM STATIONS TO PEOPLE: transmitters sharing programmes, then people sharing contacts.
branches.cn: 从电台到人：共享节目的发射台，然后是共享关系的人。

branches.en: TECHNICAL GRIDS: computers exchanging data, and utility lines carrying power or signals.
branches.cn: 技术性网络：交换数据的计算机，以及输送电力或信号的公用线路。

branches.en: THE OLD VERBS: covering with netting, and sending a programme through many stations.
branches.cn: 较早的动词：用网覆盖，以及通过多家电台播送节目。

branches.en: THE MODERN VERBS: linking machines, and cultivating a personal web of contacts.
branches.cn: 现代动词：连接机器，以及经营个人的关系网。

intro.en: Network is the compound net plus work, with no Latin suffix. English adds -ing, -ed, -er and -able to it, and the same net appears in internet, intranet, netting and netbook.
intro.cn: network 是 net 加 work 的复合词，不含拉丁后缀。英语在它上面加 -ing、-ed、-er、-able，而同一个 net 也出现在 internet、intranet、netting、netbook 中。

latinIntro.en: Network is Germanic, not Latin. The Latin entries below are its nearest counterparts, given for contrast: rete 'net', nexus 'a binding', and nectere 'to bind'.
latinIntro.cn: network 属日耳曼语，不属拉丁语。下面列出的拉丁词是它最接近的对应词，仅供对照：rete“网”、nexus“联结”、nectere“捆缚”。

items.meaning: a mesh-like structure or connected system
items.meaningCN: 网状结构；相连的系统（net“网”+ work“制成品”）
items.example: The city's tram network covers the whole centre.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市的有轨电车网络覆盖了整个市中心。

items.meaning: the act of linking systems or building contacts
items.meaningCN: 联网；建立人脉（-ing 构成动名词）
items.example: Networking is half of the value of a conference.
items.exampleCN: 建立人脉是一场会议一半的价值。

items.meaningCN: 联网的；连成网的（-ed 构成形容词）

items.meaning: a person skilled at building contacts
items.meaningCN: 善于建立人脉的人（-er 构成人称名词）
items.example: She is the best networker in the sales team.
items.exampleCN: 她是销售团队里最会经营人脉的人。

items.meaning: a mesh of cord used to catch things
items.meaningCN: 网；罗网（network 的第一成分）
items.example: The fishermen repaired the net before dawn.
items.exampleCN: 渔民在黎明前修补了渔网。

items.meaningCN: 网材；网（-ing 构成材料名词）
items.example: Netting protected the young trees from deer.
items.exampleCN: 网罩保护了小树不被鹿啃食。

items.meaningCN: 互联网（inter-“在……之间”+ net“网络”）
items.example: The files were sent over the internet.

items.meaning: a private network inside an organisation
items.meaningCN: 内联网（intra-“在内部”+ net“网络”）
items.example: Staff read the policy on the company intranet.
items.exampleCN: 员工在公司内联网上读到这项政策。

items.meaning: a small laptop designed mainly for online use
items.meaningCN: 上网本（net“网络”+ book，指主要用于上网的小电脑）
