senses.title: Alchemical balance: opposing elements in proportion
senses.titleCN: 炼金术的平衡：对立元素按比例相抵
senses.definition: in alchemy, of a substance made from opposing elements that balance each other exactly
senses.definitionCN: 在炼金术中，指由相互对立的元素按比例恰好相抵而成的物质
senses.example: Alchemists called a body neutral when fire and water balanced in it.
senses.exampleCN: 当火与水在物体中相抵平衡时，炼金术士称该物体为 neutral。
senses.why: Neutral is first recorded in the 1540s in alchemy, where opposite qualities were thought to cancel each other. The core picture is a scale that stops exactly in the middle.
senses.whyCN: neutral 最早记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，用于炼金术，当时认为对立的性质会相互抵消。核心画面是一架恰好停在正中的天平。

senses.title: Not taking sides: outside a conflict
senses.definition: not supporting either party in a dispute, war, or argument
senses.definitionCN: 在争端、战争或争论中不支持任何一方
senses.example: The referee stayed neutral and let both sides speak.
senses.exampleCN: 裁判保持中立，让双方都把话说完了。
senses.why: The alchemical balance became a social one: two opposing sides cancel, and the person in the middle belongs to neither. This sense is recorded alongside the first.
senses.whyCN: 炼金术的平衡变成了社会的平衡：两个对立面相互抵消，中间的人不属于任何一边。这个义项与最早义项同时被记录。

senses.title: Chemistry: neither acid nor alkaline
senses.definition: of a solution, having a pH near seven, neither acidic nor basic
senses.definitionCN: 指溶液 pH 接近七，既非酸性也非碱性
senses.example: Pure water is neutral, with a pH close to seven.
senses.exampleCN: 纯水是中性的，pH 接近七。
senses.why: Chemistry took the balance image literally: acid and alkali cancel, and the middle point is neutral. The sense is recorded from the 1660s.
senses.whyCN: 化学把这个平衡意象落到实处：酸与碱相抵，中间点就是中性。该义项记录于 17 世纪 60 年代。

senses.title: Not a belligerent: outside the war
senses.titleCN: 非交战国：站在战争之外
senses.definition: of a country or ship, not belonging to either side in a war
senses.definitionCN: 指国家或船只不属于战争中的任何一方
senses.example: Neutral shipping was allowed through the blockade.
senses.exampleCN: 中立国的船只被允许通过封锁线。
senses.why: A state can hold the same position as the referee: it takes no side, so its ships and ports stay outside the fighting. The sense is recorded from 1711.
senses.whyCN: 国家可以处在和裁判相同的位置：不选边，因此它的船只与港口留在战斗之外。该义项记录于 1711 年。

senses.title: Colour: low saturation, easy to live with
senses.definition: of a colour, muted and close to grey or beige, used as a quiet base
senses.definitionCN: 指颜色柔和、接近灰或米色，用作安静的底色
senses.example: The room was painted in neutral greys and warm beiges.
senses.exampleCN: 房间刷成了中性灰和暖米色。
senses.why: A muted colour sits between the strong hues and commits to none. The balance image moves from substances to light, and the sense is recorded from 1821.
senses.whyCN: 柔和的颜色处在各种强烈色相之间，不偏向任何一种。平衡意象从物质移到光线，该义项记录于 1821 年。

senses.title: Electrical neutrality: no net charge
senses.definition: having equal positive and negative charge, so that no net charge remains
senses.definitionCN: 正负电荷相等，因此没有净电荷残留
senses.example: A neutron carries no charge and is electrically neutral.
senses.exampleCN: 中子不带电荷，是电中性的。
senses.why: Positive and negative charges cancel exactly as acid and alkali cancel. The word's balance is now counted in charge rather than in qualities.
senses.whyCN: 正负电荷的相抵，正如酸与碱的相抵。这个词的平衡现在以电荷计算，而不是以性质计算。

senses.title: A neutral party: the person or state in the middle
senses.titleCN: 中立的一方：处在中间的人或国家
senses.definition: a person, country, or place that takes no side, often chosen to host talks
senses.definitionCN: 不选边的人、国家或地点，常被选作会谈地点
senses.example: The talks were held in a neutral, far from both capitals.
senses.exampleCN: 会谈在一个远离两国首都的中立地点举行。
senses.why: The adjective becomes a noun for the party that holds the middle position. Recorded as a noun in the mid-15c., it names whoever the balance leaves uncommitted.
senses.whyCN: 形容词转成名词，指占据中间位置的一方。该名词义在 15 世纪中期已有记录，命名的是被天平留在“未承诺”状态的那一方。

senses.title: Mechanical neutral: no gear engaged
senses.titleCN: 机械空挡：没有齿轮咬合
senses.definition: of a gearbox, in the position where no gear is engaged and no power reaches the wheels
senses.definitionCN: 指变速器处在没有齿轮咬合、动力不传到车轮的位置
senses.example: He shifted into neutral and let the car roll to a stop.
senses.exampleCN: 他挂入空挡，让车滑行到停下。
senses.why: In a gearbox the middle position transmits nothing: neither forward nor reverse. The sense, recorded from 1905, is the balance image in metal.
senses.whyCN: 在变速器里，中间位置什么也不传递：既不前进也不后退。该义项记录于 1905 年，是平衡意象在金属中的版本。

senses.title: Grammatical neuter: neither masculine nor feminine
senses.titleCN: 语法中性：既非阳性也非阴性
senses.definition: in grammar, of a gender that is neither masculine nor feminine
senses.definitionCN: 在语法中，指既非阳性也非阴性的性
senses.example: Latin bellum, meaning war, is a neuter noun.
senses.exampleCN: 拉丁语 bellum（战争）是一个中性名词。
senses.why: Latin neuter means 'neither the one nor the other of two'. Grammar applies that either-or refusal to gender, so a noun can stand outside the pair.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 neuter 意为“两者皆非”。语法把这种“两个都不是”的拒绝用在性上，于是名词可以站在这对选项之外。

senses.title: Neutral tone: plain and non-committal
senses.definition: of language or manner, plain and without emotion, giving nothing away
senses.definitionCN: 指语言或态度平实、不带情绪，不透露立场
senses.example: She answered in a neutral tone that gave nothing away.
senses.exampleCN: 她用一种不露声色的中性语气回答。
senses.why: A neutral colour commits to no hue, and a neutral tone commits to no side. The same middle position is applied to speech.
senses.whyCN: 中性色不对任何色相表态，中性语气也不对任何一方表态。同一个“中间位置”被用到了言语上。

intro.en: Neutral is recorded in the 1540s, first in alchemy for a balance of opposing elements, and almost at once for a person who takes no side. Latin neutralis goes back to neuter 'neither the one nor the other', probably a calque of Greek oudeteros.
intro.cn: neutral 记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，最初用于炼金术中对立元素的平衡，几乎同时就用于不选边的人。拉丁语 neutralis 可追溯至 neuter“两者皆非”，很可能是希腊语 oudeteros 的仿译。

items.en: First recorded in the 1540s in alchemy, for a substance in which opposing elements balance, and for the sense 'not taking sides'.
items.cn: 最早记录于 16 世纪 40 年代，用于炼金术中对立元素相衡的物质，同时也有“不选边”义。

items.en: By the 1550s the word is used of persons who do not join either party in a quarrel.
items.cn: 到 16 世纪 50 年代，这个词已用于不加入争吵任何一方的人。

items.en: Latin neutralis comes from neuter 'neither the one nor the other, neither of two': ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of two'. It is probably a calque of Greek oudeteros.
items.cn: 拉丁语 neutralis 来自 neuter“两者皆非、两者都不是”：ne-“不”加 uter“两者之一”。它很可能是希腊语 oudeteros 的仿译。

items.en: The two parts are PIE *ne- 'not' and the stem behind uter 'either', which is related to English whether.
items.cn: 两个部分分别是原始印欧语 *ne-“不”与 uter“两者之一”背后的词干，后者与英语 whether 同源。

items.en: Chemistry adopts the word in the 1660s for 'neither acid nor alkaline'; the sense 'not a belligerent' follows in 1711 and the colour sense in 1821.
items.cn: 化学在 17 世纪 60 年代采用这个词，表示“非酸非碱”；“非交战国”义随后于 1711 年出现，颜色义于 1821 年出现。

items.en: The noun is recorded in the mid-15c.; mechanical neutral appears in 1905, and the neutral particle the neutron takes the word into physics.
items.cn: 名词义在 15 世纪中期已有记录；机械空挡义出现于 1905 年，而中性粒子 neutron 把这个词带进了物理学。

note.en: The first group is chosen for spelling and scientific kinship, the second for the idea of not taking a side.
note.cn: 第一组按拼写与科学上的亲缘关系挑选，第二组按“不选边”的意思挑选。

entries.definition: grammatically neither masculine nor feminine. It is the Latin source word neuter, from which neutralis was formed.
entries.definitionCN: 语法上既非阳性也非阴性的。它就是拉丁语源词 neuter，neutralis 由它构成。

entries.definition: existing in nature, not made by people. It starts from Latin natura 'birth', not from neuter.
entries.definitionCN: 自然的；天生的。它来自拉丁语 natura“出生”，不是来自 neuter。

entries.definition: a particle with no electric charge. Its name was coined from neutral plus -on.
entries.definitionCN: 不带电的粒子。它的名字由 neutral 加 -on 造出。

entries.definition: not favouring one side unfairly. It judges fairly between parties, while neutral can also mean simply staying out.
entries.definitionCN: 公正的；不偏不倚的。它在两方之间公正判断，而 neutral 也可以只是置身事外。

entries.definition: showing no interest or concern. It describes unconcern, while neutral describes a balanced position between sides.
entries.definitionCN: 漠不关心的。它描述的是不关心，而 neutral 描述的是在两方之间的平衡位置。

entries.definition: of a state, not formally allied to any major power bloc. It is a political term, narrower than neutral.
entries.definitionCN: 不结盟的。它指国家不正式加入任何大国集团，是政治术语，范围比 neutral 窄。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: ne- plus uter inside neuter, the Latin source neutralis, and the dated scientific senses that followed.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：neuter 内部的 ne- 加 uter、拉丁语来源 neutralis，以及随后有年代可查的科学义项。

normal.en: ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of two' makes 'neither of the two': the middle position is built into the word.
normal.cn: ne-“不”加 uter“两者之一”就是“两者皆非”：中间位置被造进了这个词里。

normal.en: Alchemy gave the first sense, a balance of opposing elements; chemistry kept the picture as neither acid nor alkaline.
normal.cn: 炼金术给了第一个义项，即对立元素的平衡；化学保留这幅画，表示非酸非碱。

normal.en: A neutral country and a neutral referee hold the same spot: outside the two sides.
normal.cn: 中立国与中立裁判站的是同一个位置：在两方之外。

normal.en: Neutral grey commits to no hue, just as a neutral tone commits to no opinion.
normal.cn: 中性灰不对任何色相表态，正如中性语气不对任何观点表态。

normal.en: A gearbox in neutral transmits nothing: the balance image appears again in metal.
normal.cn: 处于空挡的变速器什么也不传递：平衡意象又一次出现在金属里。

abstract.en: A tug-of-war rope whose red marker hangs exactly on the centre line: both teams pull, the marker stays.
abstract.cn: 拔河绳上的红布恰好停在中心线上：两队都在拉，红布不动。

abstract.en: Two arrows pushing a ball from opposite sides with equal force: the ball does not move.
abstract.cn: 两支箭头从相反方向用同样的力推一个球：球不移动。

abstract.en: A switch resting in the middle between on and off: no current, no direction, no commitment.
abstract.cn: 一个停在“开”与“关”正中的开关：没有电流、没有方向、没有承诺。

examples.en: The mediator remained neutral even when one side raised its voice.
examples.cn: 即使一方提高了嗓门，调解人仍然保持中立。

examples.en: Choose a neutral wall colour so the furniture can change later.
examples.cn: 选一种中性的墙面颜色，以后换家具也容易搭配。

examples.en: The country declared itself neutral at the start of the war.
examples.cn: 这个国家在战争开始时宣布中立。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「牛戳」——牛站在两方中间，哪边都不戳、不顶 → neutral 中立的、中性的

root: 源自拉丁语 neutralis，来自 neuter“两者皆非”＝ ne-“不”＋ uter“两者之一”；uter 与 whether 同源，很可能是希腊语 oudeteros 的仿译。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of neutral all come from a single position: exactly in the middle, committed to neither side. Alchemy applied it to elements, politics to parties, chemistry to acids, physics to charge, grammar to gender, and speech to tone.
sensesIntro.cn: neutral 的十个义项都来自同一个位置：恰在正中，不属于任何一边。炼金术把它用在元素上，政治用在阵营上，化学用在酸碱上，物理用在电荷上，语法用在性上，言语用在语气上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tug-of-war marker stopped exactly on the centre line.
core.cn: 核心意象：拔河绳上的标记恰好停在中心线上。

branches.en: THE BALANCED MIDDLE: opposing elements in alchemy, and opposing parties in a dispute.
branches.cn: 平衡的中间：炼金术中的对立元素，以及争端中的对立两方。

branches.en: SCIENTIFIC NEUTRALITY: neither acid nor alkaline, and no net electric charge.
branches.cn: 科学上的中性：非酸非碱，以及净电荷为零。

branches.en: THE UNCOMMITTED PARTY: a state outside a war, and the person or place chosen to host talks.
branches.cn: 未承诺的一方：战争之外的国家，以及被选作会谈地点的人或地方。

branches.en: THE QUIET SURFACE: low-saturation colour, and a tone that gives nothing away.
branches.cn: 安静的表层：低彩度的颜色，以及不透露立场的语气。

branches.en: NEITHER ENGAGED NOR EITHER: a gearbox in neutral, and a grammatical gender outside the pair.
branches.cn: 既不咬合也不属于任何一边：空挡的变速器，以及跳出阴阳两性的语法中性。

intro.en: Neutral is Latin neutralis plus -al, from neuter. English builds neutrality, neutrally, neutralize, neutralization, neutralist and neutralism, and the same stem gives neuter and neutron.
intro.cn: neutral 是拉丁语 neutralis 加 -al，源自 neuter。英语构造出 neutrality、neutrally、neutralize、neutralization、neutralist、neutralism，同一词干还给出 neuter 与 neutron。

latinIntro.en: Latin neutralis 'of the neuter gender, neutral' comes from neuter 'neither of two', itself ne- 'not' plus uter 'either of two'.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 neutralis“中性的、中立的”来自 neuter“两者皆非”，后者由 ne-“不”加 uter“两者之一”构成。

items.meaning: taking no side; neither one nor the other
items.meaningCN: 中立的；中性的（-al 构成形容词）
items.example: The village stayed neutral during the dispute.
items.exampleCN: 争端期间这个村子保持中立。

items.meaning: the state of taking no side
items.meaningCN: 中立；中性（-ity 构成状态名词）
items.example: The treaty guaranteed the neutrality of the port.
items.exampleCN: 条约保障了该港口的中立地位。

items.meaningCN: 中立地；平淡地（-ly 构成副词）
items.example: She described the quarrel neutrally, naming no culprit.
items.exampleCN: 她中立地描述了这场争吵，没有指名任何一方。

items.meaning: to cancel the effect of something
items.meaningCN: 使中和；抵消（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The base neutralizes the acid almost instantly.

items.meaning: the act of cancelling or balancing
items.meaningCN: 中和作用；抵消（-ation 构成过程名词）
items.example: The neutralization produced ordinary salt and water.
items.exampleCN: 中和反应生成了普通的盐和水。

items.meaningCN: 中立主义者（-ist 构成人名名词）
items.example: The neutralists opposed joining either alliance.
items.exampleCN: 中立主义者反对加入任何一个联盟。

items.meaning: the policy of staying outside rival blocs
items.meaningCN: 中立主义（-ism 构成主张名词）
items.example: Neutralism shaped the country's foreign policy.
items.exampleCN: 中立主义塑造了该国的外交政策。

items.meaningCN: 中性的；既非阳也非阴（ne-“不”+ uter“两者之一”）
items.example: The Latin word for leaf is neuter.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语中“叶子”这个词是中性名词。

items.meaning: a particle with no electric charge
items.meaningCN: 中子（neutral 加粒子后缀 -on，指不带电的粒子）
items.example: A neutron passes through the electric field undeflected.
items.exampleCN: 中子穿过电场时不发生偏转。

items.meaningCN: 中和剂；抵消物（-er 构成施动物名词）
items.example: The lab keeps a neutralizer beside every acid bath.
items.exampleCN: 实验室在每个酸槽旁都放一瓶中和剂。

latinEntries.meaning: neither the one nor the other

latinEntries.meaningCN: 两者之一（与英语 whether 同源）

definition_zh: 从不；永不；绝不；（表示惊讶）不会吧
definition_en: at no time in the past or future, and also used to refuse something emphatically or to show surprise
core_image: 一条两头都被封死的时间线，任何一个时刻都走不进去
scene: 深夜的电话铃一直没响，他盯着屏幕，心里明白那个人再也不会打来了。She never called back after that night.
sceneCN: 这里 never 是「从不、一次也没有」（第 2 个义项：在任何场合都没有发生）；句意为那一夜之后她再也没回电话。图中可辨识物件：暗着的手机屏、没有来电的空桌面。

pos.zh: 从不；永不；绝不

derivatives.zh: 由 never 与 the less 组合而成，义为「尽管如此」
由 never 与 more 组合，书面语，义为「不再；永不再」
由 never 与 ending 复合，义为「没完没了的」

senses.title: At no time in the past or future
senses.definition: at no time, whether in the past or in the future
senses.definitionCN: 在过去或将来的任何一个时刻都不
senses.example: I have never been to that city.
senses.exampleCN: 我从未去过那座城市。
senses.why: The word welds an Old English negative particle onto ever, so it closes every point of the timeline at once instead of denying one event.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把古英语的否定小词焊在 ever（任何时候）上，于是一次性封住了时间线上的每一个点，而不是只否定某一件事。

senses.title: On no occasion; not once
senses.definition: not on a single occasion, even when the chance keeps coming back
senses.definitionCN: 即使机会反复出现，也一次都没有发生过
senses.example: She never misses a chance to help a neighbour.
senses.exampleCN: 她从不错过帮助邻居的机会。
senses.why: Because the negative is attached to ever rather than to one occasion, it runs through every repetition and finds none of them.
senses.whyCN: 否定词挂在「任何时候」上，而不是挂在某一次机会上，所以它把所有重复出现的场合都数了一遍，结论是一个也没有。

senses.title: Emphatic refusal or denial
senses.definition: used for a strong refusal or to say that something will certainly not happen
senses.definitionCN: 用于强烈拒绝，或表示某事肯定不会发生
senses.example: Never tell him that password.
senses.exampleCN: 绝对不要把那个密码告诉他。
senses.why: A refusal needs the heaviest word available, and a word that rules out every moment serves as a flat and final no.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝需要最有分量的词，而一个排除掉所有时刻的词，正好等于一句毫无余地的「不」。

senses.title: Surprise or disbelief
senses.definition: used alone or with a question to show that something is hard to believe
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用或跟疑问句，表示觉得某事难以置信
senses.example: Never! You cannot mean that.
senses.exampleCN: 不会吧！你不可能是那个意思。
senses.why: When a listener repeats the word on its own, the term that normally blocks time now blocks belief, and the denial turns into an exclamation.
senses.whyCN: 当听者把这个词单独喊出来时，这个平时封锁时间的词转而封锁「相信」，否定就变成了一声惊叹。

intro.en: Never is an Old English compound of a negative particle and the word for ever, and it has kept that shape for more than a thousand years.
intro.cn: never 是古英语中否定小词与「任何时候」一词的复合，这个结构保持了一千多年。

items.en: The recorded form nǣfre already meant at no time, built from ne plus ǣfre.
items.cn: 有记录的 nǣfre 已经表示「在任何时候都不」，由 ne 与 ǣfre 合成。

items.en: Ne was the general negative particle placed before another word to deny it.
items.cn: ne 是通用的否定小词，放在另一个词前面表示否定。

items.en: Āfre meant at any time and is the same word that became modern ever.
items.cn: āfre 意为「在任何时候」，也就是现代英语 ever 的前身。

items.en: Middle English spelled the word never or ner and used it for past time as well as for strong refusals.
items.cn: 中古英语把它写作 never 或 ner，既用于过去时间，也用于强烈的拒绝。

items.en: Modern English keeps the compound as one word and adds fixed phrases such as never mind and never again.
items.cn: 现代英语把这个复合词固定为一个词，并发展出 never mind、never again 等固定说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on ever, the second half of never; the near-meaning group gathers words about frequency and its opposite.
note.cn: 形近组收以 ever（never 的后半部分）为核心构成的词；近义组收与频率及其反义有关的词。

entries.definition: At any time; the word that supplies the second half of never.
entries.definitionCN: 在任何时候；正是它提供了 never 的后半部分。

entries.definition: At any time that something happens; built on ever.
entries.definitionCN: 每当某事发生时；由 ever 构成。

entries.definition: In spite of that; formed from never, the and less.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管如此；由 never、the 与 less 组合而成。

entries.definition: For all future time; a literary word built on ever.
entries.definitionCN: 永远；书面语，由 ever 构成。

entries.definition: At every time; the direct opposite of never.
entries.definitionCN: 总是；每时每刻，正好是 never 的反面。

entries.definition: On only a few occasions, but not never.
entries.definitionCN: 很少；只有少数几次，但不是一次也没有。

entries.definition: Almost never, used when something happens very few times.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎从不；表示某事发生的次数极少。

entries.definition: Almost not at all, close to never in everyday speech.
entries.definitionCN: 几乎不；在日常口语里接近 never。

normalIntro.en: The word is a negative particle and ever fused together, so most of its family keeps circling the idea of no moment at all.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由否定小词与 ever 融合而成，所以它的词族大多围绕「没有任何一个时刻」打转。

normal.en: Split never into ne plus ever: not ever, at no time.
normal.cn: 把 never 拆成 ne 加 ever：任何时候都不，也就是从不。

normal.en: The ever inside never is the same ever you use in questions such as have you ever.
normal.cn: never 里的 ever，就是你在 have you ever 这类问句里用的那个 ever。

normal.en: Since Middle English the two parts have been written as one word, unlike most other ne compounds.
normal.cn: 从中古英语起，这两部分就写成一个词，和大多数其他带 ne 的复合词不同。

normal.en: The phrase never mind uses the same word to cancel a topic rather than a moment.
normal.cn: never mind 里用的是同一个词，只是它取消的是一个话题，而不是一个时刻。

normal.en: Fixed pairs such as never again and almost never show how firmly the word locks a time span.
normal.cn: never again、almost never 这类固定组合，显示出这个词把一段时间锁得多么死。

abstract.en: A word that denies every point of time at once is stronger than a word that denies one event.
abstract.cn: 一个能同时否定时间线上每个点的词，比只否定一件事的词要强硬得多。

abstract.en: When the same word later denies belief instead of time, you can hear how easily a closed door becomes an exclamation.
abstract.cn: 当同一个词后来否定的是「相信」而不是时间，你能听出一扇关死的门多么容易变成一声惊叹。

abstract.en: Never is a reminder that some doors are not merely shut for now; they are shut on every side.
abstract.cn: never 提醒人：有些门不是暂时关上，而是四面都封死了。

examples.en: I have never seen snow fall in this city.
examples.cn: 我从未见过这座城市下雪。

examples.en: Never open that door while the alarm is on.
examples.cn: 警报开着的时候绝对不要开那扇门。

examples.en: She never misses a chance to help a neighbour.
examples.cn: 她从不错过帮助邻居的机会。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「捏我」——他捏了我一下，我记住了：这种事「从不」再犯。

root: 古英语 ne（否定）加 ǣfre（在任何时候）合成 nǣfre，意为「任何时候都不」；拉丁语中没有可靠的同源同族词。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is no moment at all; the senses then widen from repeated occasions to flat refusal and finally to disbelief.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「没有任何一个时刻」；义项由此从反复出现的场合，扩展到断然拒绝，最后到难以置信。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a timeline sealed at both ends so that no moment can be entered.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条两头都封死的时间线，任何一个时刻都走不进去。

branches.en: a timeline with every point crossed out
branches.cn: 整条时间线上的每个点都被划掉

branches.en: a calendar of chances without a single check mark
branches.cn: 一页机会的日历，没有一个打勾

branches.en: a hand raised flat in refusal
branches.cn: 一只平举的手表示拒绝

branches.en: a face repeating the word in shock
branches.cn: 一张震惊地重复这个词的脸

branches.en: one denial serving both past time and every repeated occasion
branches.cn: 同一个否定，既用于过去，也用于反复出现的场合

intro.en: The word is held together by an Old English negative particle, the word for ever, their fused form, and a few modern compounds.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语否定小词、表示 ever 的词、二者融合的形式，以及几个现代复合词共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin cognate is recorded; the first element is an Old English negative particle, not a Latin one.
latinIntro.cn: 没有可靠的拉丁同族词记录；它的第一个成分是古英语的否定小词，而不是拉丁语的。

items.meaning: forming words such as whoever and whatever
items.meaningCN: 构成 whoever、whatever 等词的后缀

items.meaning: in spite of that, built on never
items.meaningCN: 尽管如此，由 never 加 the less 构成
items.exampleCN: 尽管如此，她仍继续前行。

definition_zh: 然而；尽管如此；不过
definition_en: in spite of that; however; used to introduce a statement that stands despite what came before
core_image: 门上挂着“禁止进入”的牌子，人还是推门走了进去
scene: 小路封了，一半还泡着水，徒步者却还是跨过告示牌继续走。The trail is closed and half flooded; nevertheless, a hiker steps past the sign and walks on.
sceneCN: 这里 nevertheless 是「尽管如此、仍然」（第 1 个义项：让步之后仍然成立）；句意：步道已经封闭、有一半被水淹，尽管如此，一名徒步者还是绕过告示牌继续往前走。图中可辨识物件：封闭告示牌、积水步道、徒步者的登山杖、黄黑警示带；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 然而；尽管如此；不过（连接性副词，承接前文并转折）

collocations.zh: 尽管如此，事实仍然不变

derivatives.zh: 尽管如此（同构的并列复合词，用 none 代替 never）
从不；决不（构词成分，此处原义为“一点也不”）
曾经；无论何时（never 的第二成分）
更少的；更少地（构词成分，比较级）
除非（同出 less 的复合连词）
减少；减轻（less 加 -en 构成的动词）

senses.title: In spite of that: opening a sentence against expectation
senses.titleCN: 尽管如此：开门见山地逆着预期说
senses.definition: used at the start of a sentence to say that what follows is true in spite of what was just said
senses.definitionCN: 用于句首，表示接下来的内容尽管有前文所说的情况仍然成立
senses.example: The hotel was full. Nevertheless, we found a room nearby.
senses.exampleCN: 旅馆客满了。尽管如此，我们还是在附近找到了一间房。
senses.why: Nevertheless is never plus the less, literally 'not any the less'. What came before does not make the next statement any smaller, so the sentence opens by refusing to be reduced.
senses.whyCN: nevertheless 是 never 加 the less，字面是“一点也不因此减少”。前文并没有让后一句变小，所以这个句子一开口就拒绝被削减。

senses.title: Joining two clauses after a semicolon
senses.definition: used after a semicolon to link two clauses and mark the second as a contrast
senses.definitionCN: 用于分号之后连接两个小句，并标记后一句为转折
senses.example: The evidence was thin; nevertheless, the jury convicted.
senses.exampleCN: 证据薄弱；尽管如此，陪审团仍判定有罪。
senses.why: As a conjunctive adverb it carries the contrast across the punctuation. The 'not any the less' still measures the second clause against the first.
senses.whyCN: 作为连接性副词，它把转折跨过标点带过去。“一点也不因此减少”仍在用前一句来衡量后一句。

senses.title: After but: the doubled contrast
senses.titleCN: 跟在 but 之后：双重的转折
senses.definition: used with but to add emphasis, as in 'cheap but nevertheless good'
senses.definitionCN: 与 but 连用以加强转折，如 cheap but nevertheless good
senses.example: The plan was expensive but nevertheless worth every penny.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划很贵，但尽管如此，每一分钱都值得。
senses.why: But already turns the sentence; nevertheless adds that the earlier fact does not reduce the later one. The two markers reinforce rather than contradict each other.
senses.whyCN: but 已经让句子转向；nevertheless 再补上一层：前面的事实并不能削减后面的事实。两个标记是相互加强，而不是相互矛盾。

senses.title: At the end: a trailing afterthought
senses.titleCN: 放在句尾：事后的补一句
senses.definition: placed at the end of a clause to add a delayed contrast, often after a pause
senses.definitionCN: 放在小句末尾，补充一个迟来的转折，常出现在停顿之后
senses.example: It was a foolish plan. He went ahead, nevertheless.
senses.exampleCN: 那是个愚蠢的计划。他还是照做了，尽管如此。
senses.why: The word can trail because the comparison is still live: the action is measured against the warning and is 'none the less' for it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词可以拖在句尾，因为比较仍然有效：行动相对于警告被衡量，而它“并未因此减少”。

senses.title: Academic concession: grant the objection, keep the claim
senses.titleCN: 学术让步：承认异议，保留论点
senses.definition: used in argument to admit a limitation and still maintain the main claim
senses.definitionCN: 用于论证中，承认某项局限，同时仍然坚持主要论点
senses.example: The sample is small; nevertheless, the result is suggestive.
senses.exampleCN: 样本很小；尽管如此，这一结果仍有提示意义。
senses.why: The concession lowers the claim's strength, and nevertheless says the claim is not lowered by that amount. It is the written form of 'none the less'.
senses.whyCN: 让步降低了论点的强度，而 nevertheless 说论点并没有因此降低那么多。它就是书面语里的“none the less”。

senses.title: Personal admission: I knew, and did it anyway
senses.titleCN: 个人承认：我知道，可我还是做了
senses.definition: used to admit a fault or risk and still report the action taken
senses.definitionCN: 用于承认过错或风险，却仍然陈述已经采取的行动
senses.example: I knew the risk; nevertheless, I signed.
senses.exampleCN: 我知道有风险；尽管如此，我还是签了。
senses.why: Here the first clause is self-criticism. Nevertheless refuses to let the admission cancel the act, so the person owns both at once.
senses.whyCN: 这里前一句是自我批评。nevertheless 不让这份承认取消行动，于是这个人同时承认了两件事。

senses.title: Formal register: the steady voice of statutes
senses.titleCN: 正式语体：法条里沉稳的声音
senses.definition: used in legal, official, and technical prose as a formal alternative to 'but' or 'however'
senses.definitionCN: 在法律、公文与技术写作中作为 but 或 however 的正式替代
senses.example: The notice was defective; nevertheless, it had legal effect.
senses.exampleCN: 该通知存在瑕疵；尽管如此，它仍具有法律效力。
senses.why: The compound is long and steady, and its 'none the less' logic suits rules that survive exceptions. Formal prose prefers it to a bare but.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词长而稳，其“并未减少”的逻辑正合那些在例外之后仍然存活的规则。正式写作偏爱它，而不是光秃秃的 but。

senses.title: Narrative: obstacles listed, outcome unchanged
senses.titleCN: 叙事：障碍列举完，结果不变
senses.definition: used in storytelling after a list of difficulties to show the result still happened
senses.definitionCN: 在叙事中用于列举困难之后，表示结果仍然发生
senses.example: Rain, delays and lost luggage — nevertheless, they arrived on time.
senses.exampleCN: 大雨、延误、行李丢失——尽管如此，他们还是准时到了。
senses.why: Each obstacle would normally count against the outcome. The word gathers them and says the outcome is none the less for all of them.
senses.whyCN: 每一项障碍通常都会对结果不利。这个词把它们收拢起来，说结果并没有因为这一切而减少。

senses.title: Emphatic: after an extreme list, the result still stands
senses.titleCN: 强调：极端情况之后，结果仍然成立
senses.definition: used after the strongest possible objection to insist that the result stands
senses.definitionCN: 用于最强的反对意见之后，坚持结果仍然成立
senses.example: Every forecast said failure; nevertheless, the launch succeeded.
senses.exampleCN: 所有预测都说会失败；尽管如此，发射还是成功了。
senses.why: The stronger the objection, the more the 'not any the less' has to do. Here the word is close to 'against all of it'.
senses.whyCN: 反对越强，“一点也不因此减少”要做的功就越大。这里的词义接近“对抗这一切”。

senses.title: The fixed frame: it is nevertheless true that
senses.titleCN: 固定框架：it is nevertheless true that
senses.definition: used in the frame 'it is nevertheless true that' to affirm a fact after doubt has been raised
senses.definitionCN: 用于 it is nevertheless true that 这一框架，在被质疑之后仍然肯定某一事实
senses.example: It is nevertheless true that the method saved lives.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管如此，这个方法确实救过人命，这一点是真的。
senses.why: The frame places truth itself on the far side of the contrast: whatever was argued, the fact is none the less true.
senses.whyCN: 这个框架把“真”本身放到转折的另一边：无论前面争论了什么，事实并未因此而不真。

intro.en: Nevertheless began as the phrase never the less, written neuer þe lesse in the early 14c. and joined into one word by the mid-14c. Its never does not mean 'never' but 'not at all, none the', as in never the wiser.
intro.cn: nevertheless 起初是短语 never the less，14 世纪早期写作 neuer þe lesse，到 14 世纪中期合成一词。其中的 never 不是“永不”，而是“一点也不、none the”，如 never the wiser。

items.en: First recorded in the early 14c. as the phrase neuer þe lesse, still written in separate parts.
items.cn: 最早记录于 14 世纪早期，写作短语 neuer þe lesse，各部分仍分开书写。

items.en: By the mid-14c. the parts are joined as neuerþeles, and the word begins to work as a single adverb.
items.cn: 到 14 世纪中期，各部分合成 neuerþeles，这个词开始作为单一副词使用。

items.en: Middle English also had neverthelater, never-less, ner-the-less, never-later and not-the-less, all built on the same 'none the less' pattern.
items.cn: 中古英语还有 neverthelater、never-less、ner-the-less、never-later、not-the-less 等变体，都建立在同一个“none the less”模式上。

items.en: Never comes from Old English næfre, itself ne 'not' plus æfre 'ever'.
items.cn: never 来自古英语 næfre，本身由 ne“不”加 æfre“曾经”构成。

items.en: Modern English keeps nevertheless beside nonetheless; the two are parallel compounds, one with never and one with none.
items.cn: 现代英语让 nevertheless 与 nonetheless 并存；两者是并列复合词，一个用 never，一个用 none。

note.en: The first group shares the never-the-less shape or its parts, the second shares the contrastive meaning.
note.cn: 第一组共享 never-the-less 的结构或其组成部分，第二组共享转折的词义。

entries.definition: in spite of that. It is built exactly like nevertheless but with none instead of never, and the two are interchangeable.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管如此。它的构造与 nevertheless 完全相同，只是用 none 代替 never，两者可以互换。

entries.definition: the older phrase written in separate words. It shows the literal parts: never, the, less.
entries.definitionCN: 分开书写的较早短语。它显示了这个词的字面成分：never、the、less。

entries.definition: an obsolete variant of nevertheless, built with later instead of less. It shows how freely the pattern was varied.
entries.definitionCN: nevertheless 的废弃变体，用 later 而不是 less。它说明这个模式当年被替换得多么自由。

entries.definition: in whatever way, or used to introduce a contrast. It is the general-purpose connector, while nevertheless is heavier and more formal.
entries.definitionCN: 无论如何；然而。它是通用连接词，而 nevertheless 更重、更正式。

entries.definition: in spite of; despite. It often works as a preposition or a formal connector, and is even heavier than nevertheless.
entries.definitionCN: 尽管；虽然。它常作介词或正式连接词，比 nevertheless 还要重。

entries.definition: in spite of that, used in speech. It carries the same turn but sounds conversational rather than written.
entries.definitionCN: 即使如此。它带有同样的转折，但听起来是口语而非书面语。

normalIntro.en: These links are real: never here means 'not at all', less is a comparative, and the Middle English variants all repeat the same pattern.
normalIntro.cn: 这些联想都是真实的：这里的 never 意为“一点也不”，less 是比较级，而中古英语的各种变体都重复同一个模式。

normal.en: Never in this word is not 'never': it means 'not at all, none the', as in never the wiser or never the worse.
normal.cn: 这个词里的 never 不是“永不”：它意为“一点也不、none the”，如 never the wiser、never the worse。

normal.en: the less is a comparative. Together the parts say 'not any the less', which is why the later clause is not reduced.
normal.cn: the less 是比较级。合起来说“一点也不因此减少”，这正是后一句没有被削减的原因。

normal.en: Middle English had neverthelater, never-less, ner-the-less and not-the-less, all variations on the same comparison.
normal.cn: 中古英语有 neverthelater、never-less、ner-the-less、not-the-less，都是同一个比较结构的变体。

normal.en: Nonetheless is the twin: same building plan, with none instead of never.
normal.cn: nonetheless 是它的双胞胎：同样的建筑图纸，只用 none 代替 never。

normal.en: But nevertheless is a standard frame: but turns the sentence, nevertheless insists nothing was lost in the turn.
normal.cn: but nevertheless 是标准框架：but 让句子转向，nevertheless 坚持这次转向没有损失任何东西。

abstract.en: A door marked NO ENTRY, already pushed half open: the warning is real, and the step is still taken.
abstract.cn: 一扇写着“禁止入内”的门已被推开一半：警告是真的，脚步还是迈了出去。

abstract.en: A line that bends at an obstacle and then continues in the same direction: the bend does not shorten the road.
abstract.cn: 一条线在障碍处弯了一下，然后继续朝同一方向走：弯折并没有让路变短。

abstract.en: A hand pressing down on a box while another hand still lifts it: the weight is counted, and the lift still happens.
abstract.cn: 一只手向下压箱子，另一只手仍把它抬起：重量被算进去了，抬起仍然发生。

examples.en: The instructions were unclear; nevertheless, the team finished on time.
examples.cn: 说明不清楚；尽管如此，团队还是按时完成了。

examples.en: He was warned about the ice, but nevertheless he walked out onto the lake.
examples.cn: 有人警告过他冰面危险，但尽管如此，他还是走上了湖面。

examples.en: It is nevertheless true that the old bridge has carried the town's traffic for a century.
examples.cn: 尽管如此，这座老桥确实已经承载了小镇一个世纪的交通，这一点是真的。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「那我也赖着」——尽管被赶、被劝，那我也赖着不走 → nevertheless 尽管如此、仍然

root: 由 never“一点也不、none the”＋ the ＋ less（比较级）构成的复合副词，14 世纪早期写作 neuer þe lesse；never 来自古英语 næfre＝ ne“不”＋ æfre“曾经”。

sensesIntro.en: Ten senses of nevertheless all carry one comparison: whatever was said, the next statement is 'none the less'. The word changes position and register, from sentence opening to trailing afterthought, from academic concession to legal prose.
sensesIntro.cn: nevertheless 的十个义项都带着同一个比较：无论前面说了什么，后一句都“并未因此减少”。这个词改变的是位置与语体，从句首到句尾补语，从学术让步到法律文书。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a closed sign on a door that is opened anyway.
core.cn: 核心意象：门上的封闭告示，而门还是被推开了。

branches.en: SENTENCE POSITIONS: opening a new sentence, and joining two clauses after a semicolon.
branches.cn: 句子位置：开启一个新句子，以及在分号后连接两个小句。

intro.en: Nevertheless is a compound, not a suffixed word: never plus the plus less. English keeps the same plan in nonetheless, and the parts survive separately in never, ever, less, unless and lessen.

items.meaningCN: 减少；减轻（less + -en 构成动词）

items.meaningCN: 较小的；次要的（less 再加 -er 的历史双重比较级）

scene: 校门口的牌子刚挂上去，油漆还带着光，孩子们围着它读上面的班级名。The newly opened library stands where the old bus stop used to be.

pos.zh: 新近；刚刚；以新的方式

senses.title: A short time ago
senses.definition: recently, in the short period just before now
senses.definitionCN: 最近，在过去不久的短短一段时间里
senses.example: The newly painted wall still smells of fresh paint.
senses.exampleCN: 刚刷过漆的墙还带着新漆的味道。
senses.why: New supplies the idea of something fresh, and the adverb ending turns that freshness into a statement about when it arrived.
senses.whyCN: new 提供「崭新」的底色，副词词尾把这份崭新变成对时间的说明：它是什么时候到来的。

senses.title: In a fresh or different way
senses.definition: in a way that is new, fresh or different from what came before
senses.definitionCN: 以一种新的、与以往不同的方式
senses.example: She arranged the room newly, with the desk facing the window.
senses.exampleCN: 她重新布置了房间，让书桌朝向窗户。
senses.why: Once the adverb names freshness, it can describe the manner of an action, not only the moment when it happened.
senses.whyCN: 副词一旦表示「新鲜」，就不只能说明事情发生在什么时候，也能说明它是怎么做的。

senses.title: Recently made or newly become
senses.definition: used before a past participle to mean recently made, chosen or changed into that state
senses.definitionCN: 用在过去分词前，表示最近被做成、选出或变成某种状态
senses.example: The newly elected mayor promised to repair every street in the district.
senses.exampleCN: 新当选的市长承诺修好区里的每一条街。
senses.why: Placed in front of a participle, the adverb squeezes a whole clause about a recent change into two words.
senses.whyCN: 放在分词前面时，这个副词把一个关于「最近发生变化」的完整从句压缩成两个词。

intro.en: Newly is the adjective new plus the Old English adverb ending that became modern -ly, and the pair has meant both recently and in a new way.
intro.cn: newly 是形容词 new 加上演变为现代 -ly 的古英语副词词尾，这个组合既表示「最近」，也表示「以新的方式」。

items.en: A root meaning new is widely reconstructed, though the starred form is a reconstruction rather than a recorded word.
items.cn: 表示「新」的词根一般重构为 *newo-，带星号的形式是重构，并非有记录的词。

items.en: Nīwe meant new and supplied the adjective from which the adverb was built.
items.cn: nīwe 意为「新的」，是构成这个副词的那个形容词。

items.en: The ending -līce turned adjectives into adverbs of manner and is the ancestor of modern -ly.
items.cn: -līce 把形容词变成方式副词，是现代 -ly 的祖先。

items.en: Middle English wrote the adverb as newliche or newly and kept the sense of recently.
items.cn: 中古英语把这个副词写作 newliche 或 newly，保留了「最近」的意思。

items.en: Modern English shortened the ending and extended newly to combinations such as newly built and newly elected.
items.cn: 现代英语把词尾简化，并把 newly 扩展到 newly built、newly elected 这类组合中。

senses.definitionCN: 刊登在报纸上或通过广播电视播出的近期事件报道
senses.example: The evening news covered the flood in three villages.
senses.exampleCN: 晚间新闻报道了三个村庄的洪水。
senses.why: Once fresh things are collected and published, the word moves from the information itself to the work of reporting it.
senses.whyCN: 新鲜事一旦被收集并刊播，词义就从「信息本身」转到「报道这项工作」上。

senses.title: A news programme
senses.definition: a regular television or radio programme that reports recent events
senses.definitionCN: 定期播出、报道近期事件的电视或广播节目
senses.example: She watches the news every night before bed.
senses.exampleCN: 她每晚睡前都看新闻节目。
senses.why: The same word can name the half hour on the screen because that slot is filled with nothing but collected news.
senses.whyCN: 同一个词也能指屏幕上那半小时，因为那个时段里装的正是收集起来的新闻。

senses.title: Something worth reporting
senses.titleCN: 值得报道的事；新闻素材
senses.definition: a person or event interesting enough to be reported as news
senses.definitionCN: 足够有趣、值得当作新闻来报道的人或事
senses.example: A cat stuck on a roof was the news of the week.
senses.exampleCN: 一只猫被困在屋顶上，成了本周的新闻。
senses.why: When the telling matters more than the event, the word shifts again to mean whatever supplies the story.
senses.whyCN: 当「讲出去」比「发生了什么」更重要时，词义再次偏移，转而指任何能提供故事的材料。

intro.en: News was originally the plural of the adjective new, meaning new things; the spelling and its singular, uncountable use settled in the early modern period.
intro.cn: news 原本是形容词 new 的复数，意为「新事物」；它的拼写以及单数、不可数的用法在近代早期固定下来。

items.en: The adjective nīwe meant new and could also stand as a noun for a new thing.
items.cn: 形容词 nīwe 意为「新的」，也可当名词用，指一件新事物。

items.en: Middle English used newes, the plural of new, for new things or fresh reports.
items.cn: 中古英语用 newes，即 new 的复数，指新事物或新得到的消息。

items.en: The spelling settled as news, and the word was increasingly treated as a singular mass noun.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 news，并越来越被当作不可数的单数名词使用。

items.en: News became the everyday word for printed reports and was combined with paper to form newspaper.
items.cn: news 成为印刷报道的常用词，并与 paper 组合成 newspaper。

items.en: Modern English keeps news uncountable and uses it for media reports, broadcasts and phrases such as good news.
items.cn: 现代英语让 news 保持不可数，用它指媒体报道、广播节目，以及 good news 这类说法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on new or on the news compound; the near-meaning group gathers words for information and reports.
note.cn: 形近组收以 new 或 news 复合而成的词；近义组收表示信息与报道的词。

entries.definition: Recently made; the adjective from which news was formed.
entries.definitionCN: 新近制成的；news 正是由它构成。

entries.definition: Printed sheets that carry news.
entries.definitionCN: 承载新闻的印刷纸张；报纸。

entries.definition: A radio or television broadcast of news.
entries.definitionCN: 广播或电视的新闻播报。

entries.definition: Full of news or gossip.
entries.definitionCN: 消息多；爱讲闲话。

entries.definition: Facts told or learned about something.
entries.definitionCN: 被告知或了解到的关于某事的事实。

entries.definition: A spoken or written account of an event.
entries.definitionCN: 对事件的口头或书面叙述。

entries.definition: A short official statement or news update.
entries.definitionCN: 简短的官方公告或新闻更新。

entries.definition: Old-fashioned word for news.
entries.definitionCN: 消息；旧时或书面语的说法。

normalIntro.en: The word grew out of new as a bundle of fresh things, and its family keeps connecting freshness, reporting and the media that carry it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从 new 长出来，本是一捆新鲜事；词族始终把新鲜、报道与承载报道的媒体连在一起。

normal.en: news is new plus a plural s: a bundle of new things told to others.
normal.cn: news 是 new 加复数词尾 s：把一捆新鲜事讲给别人听。

normal.en: It looks plural but takes a singular verb: the news is good.
normal.cn: 它看起来像复数，却接单数动词：the news is good。

normal.en: There is no a news; say a piece of news or a news item.
normal.cn: 不能说 a news，要说 a piece of news 或 a news item。

normal.en: Common compounds include newspaper, newscast, newsstand and newsletter.
normal.cn: 常见复合词包括 newspaper、newscast、newsstand 与 newsletter。

normal.en: Good news and bad news both stay uncountable and never take a plural verb.
normal.cn: good news 与 bad news 都保持不可数，也从不接复数动词。

abstract.en: A mass of fresh facts becomes a single uncountable word because the telling, not the counting, is what matters.
abstract.cn: 一堆新鲜事实变成一个不可数词，因为重要的是「讲出去」，而不是「数清楚」。

abstract.en: The same word can be the story, the printed page and the evening programme, because all three are ways of carrying a report.
abstract.cn: 同一个词可以指故事、印出的纸页和晚间节目，因为三者都是承载报道的方式。

abstract.en: News is freshness organised until it can travel.
abstract.cn: news 就是被整理到可以传播为止的新鲜。

examples.en: The news spread through the village before noon.
examples.cn: 消息在中午之前就传遍了村子。

examples.en: I have good news for you: the scholarship is yours.
examples.cn: 我有好消息告诉你：奖学金归你了。

examples.en: She listens to the news on the radio while cooking.
examples.cn: 她做饭时听广播里的新闻。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「纽斯」——「纽斯」是新事的声音；一条条新事凑起来，就成了新闻。

root: 中古英语 newes 是 new 的复数，本义「新的事物、新消息」；后拼作 news，被当作不可数名词。与拉丁语 novus（新）同出原始印欧语词根。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is fresh information; the senses then divide into the reports, the broadcast programme and whatever is worth reporting.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是新鲜的信息；义项由此分出报道、广播节目，以及任何值得报道的材料。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stack of fresh reports arriving at the door, still warm from the press.
core.cn: 核心意象：一叠刚送到门口的消息，油墨还没凉。

branches.en: a neighbour telling you what happened last night
branches.cn: 邻居告诉你昨晚发生了什么

branches.en: a front page filled with the flood
branches.cn: 登满洪水的头版

branches.en: a family sitting before the evening broadcast
branches.cn: 一家人坐在晚间节目前的样子

branches.en: a cat on a roof drawing a crowd
branches.cn: 屋顶上的猫引来一群人

branches.en: one word for the story, the paper and the programme
branches.cn: 同一个词，兼指故事、报纸与节目

intro.en: The word is new plus a plural ending, and its compounds pair that root with the things that carry reports.
intro.cn: 这个词是 new 加一个复数词尾，它的复合词把这个词根与承载报道的事物配在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin novus is a distant cousin through the same reconstructed root for new, not a direct source of the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 novus 通过同一个重构的「新」词根与它远亲相连，并不是这个英语词的直接来源。

definition_zh: 报纸；一份报纸；报社
definition_en: a printed publication, usually issued daily or weekly, containing news, articles and advertisements
core_image: 折叠的报纸摊在餐桌上，一角被咖啡杯压住，露出半截头条
scene: 早餐桌上一杯咖啡压着摊开的报纸，父亲边喝边翻到体育版。He reads a newspaper every morning before work.
sceneCN: 这里 newspaper 是「报纸」（第 1 个义项：刊载新闻的印刷出版物）；句意为他每天上班前都读一份报纸。图中可辨识物件：咖啡杯、摊开的报纸、餐桌。

pos.zh: 报纸；报社

derivatives.zh: 由 news 与 print 复合，义为「新闻纸」
由 newspaper 与 man 复合，义为「报人；男记者」
由 newspaper 与 woman 复合，义为「女报人；女记者」

senses.title: A printed publication with news
senses.definition: a set of printed sheets, usually published daily or weekly, containing news, articles and advertisements
senses.definitionCN: 通常每日或每周出版、刊载新闻、文章与广告的一套印刷纸张
senses.example: The newspaper printed the story on its front page.
senses.exampleCN: 那份报纸把这条新闻登在了头版。
senses.why: The compound joins news with paper, so the name literally points to the sheets that carry the reports.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把 news 与 paper 拼在一起，字面上就指向承载报道的那些纸张。

senses.title: A single copy or issue
senses.definition: one copy or one day's issue of such a publication
senses.definitionCN: 这样一份出版物的一份或某一期
senses.example: She bought a newspaper from the stand on the corner.
senses.exampleCN: 她从街角的报刊亭买了一份报纸。
senses.why: Once the sheets become a product, the same word can count them one by one in a reader's hands.
senses.whyCN: 当这些纸张变成商品，同一个词就能在读者手里把它们一份一份地数出来。

senses.title: The organization that publishes it
senses.definition: the company or office that produces a newspaper
senses.definitionCN: 生产这份报纸的公司或办公机构
senses.example: He has worked for the same newspaper for twenty years.
senses.exampleCN: 他在同一家报社工作了二十年。
senses.why: A paper is also the people who write and print it, so the word slides from the object to the institution behind it.
senses.whyCN: 一份报纸也指写它、印它的那些人，于是词义从物件滑到它背后的机构。

intro.en: Newspaper joins the English word news to paper, a word that came from Latin through Old French and named the material before it named the publication.
intro.cn: newspaper 把英语的 news 与 paper 组合起来；paper 经古法语来自拉丁语，先指材料，后指出版物。

items.en: Papyrus was the writing reed of the ancient world and gave Latin its word for paper.
items.cn: papyrus 是古代用来书写的芦苇，也是拉丁语中「纸」一词的来源。

items.en: Old French shortened papyrus into papier, the material on which words were written.
items.cn: 古法语把 papyrus 缩成 papier，指书写文字所用的材料。

items.en: Middle English paper named the material and later a sheet or a document made from it.
items.cn: 中古英语 paper 指纸张材料，后来也指用纸做成的一页或一份文件。

items.en: News and paper were combined into newspaper for the printed sheets that carried reports.
items.cn: news 与 paper 组合成 newspaper，指承载报道的印刷纸张。

items.en: Modern English uses newspaper for the printed product, a single issue and the company that publishes it.
items.cn: 现代英语用 newspaper 指印刷品、单份报纸，也指出版它的公司。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built on news or on the paper compound; the near-meaning group gathers other kinds of periodical publication.
note.cn: 形近组收以 news 或 paper 复合而成的词；近义组收其他类型的定期出版物。

entries.definition: Information about recent events; the first half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 关于近期事件的信息；这个复合词的前半部分。

entries.definition: The material made for writing and printing; the second half of the compound.
entries.definitionCN: 用于书写和印刷的材料；这个复合词的后半部分。

entries.definition: The cheap paper used for printing newspapers.
entries.definitionCN: 印刷报纸所用的廉价纸张。

entries.definition: A small stall where newspapers are sold.
entries.definitionCN: 出售报纸的小摊；报刊亭。

entries.definition: A periodical, often more serious or specialised than a newspaper.
entries.definitionCN: 定期刊物，常比报纸更严肃或更专业。

entries.definition: A small-format newspaper focused on sensation and pictures.
entries.definitionCN: 以小版面、耸动内容和图片为主的小报。

entries.definition: A large-format newspaper known for serious reporting.
entries.definitionCN: 以大版面、严肃报道著称的报纸。

entries.definition: Any publication that appears at regular intervals.
entries.definitionCN: 任何定期出版的刊物。

normalIntro.en: The word is a plain compound of news and paper, and its family keeps combining the report with the material or the place that sells it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 news 与 paper 的直接复合，词族不断把「报道」与材料或售卖地点结合起来。

normal.en: news plus paper equals the paper that carries the news.
normal.cn: news 加 paper 等于承载新闻的那种纸。

normal.en: Paper goes back to Latin papyrus, the reed once used for writing.
normal.cn: paper 可追到拉丁语 papyrus，那是古时用来书写的芦苇。

normal.en: One newspaper, two newspapers: count the physical copies with a plural.
normal.cn: one newspaper、two newspapers：用复数来数一份份实物。

normal.en: The newspaper can also mean the company, and then it takes a singular verb.
normal.cn: the newspaper 也可指公司，这时它接单数动词。

normal.en: The usual partners are daily newspaper, local newspaper and newspaper article.
normal.cn: 常见搭配有 daily newspaper、local newspaper 与 newspaper article。

abstract.en: A newspaper is news that has been given a body of paper and a daily habit.
abstract.cn: 报纸就是给新闻配上一副纸做的身体，再养成每天阅读的习惯。

abstract.en: The same word covers the object, the single copy and the institution because a paper exists only while all three hold together.
abstract.cn: 同一个词兼指物件、单份与机构，因为只有三者抱在一起，一份报纸才成立。

abstract.en: Every folded page is a day's worth of the world pressed flat.
abstract.cn: 每一页折起的纸，都是一天世界被压平的形状。

examples.en: He reads a newspaper every morning before work.
examples.cn: 他每天上班前都读一份报纸。

examples.en: The local newspaper sent a reporter to the school fair.
examples.cn: 地方报纸派了一名记者去学校集市。

examples.en: She wrapped the old plates in newspaper before putting them in the box.
examples.cn: 她用旧报纸把盘子包好，再放进箱子里。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「纽斯陪珀」——「纽斯」是新事的声音，「陪珀」是纸页的声响，合起来就是报纸。

root: news（新闻）与 paper（纸）复合；paper 源自拉丁语 papyrus（纸莎草），经古法语 papier 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is printed sheets carrying reports; the senses then move to the single copy and to the company that produces it.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是承载报道的印刷纸张；义项由此转到单份报纸，再转到生产它的公司。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a folded paper on the breakfast table, one corner held down by a coffee cup.
core.cn: 核心意象：早餐桌上折叠的报纸，一角被咖啡杯压住。

branches.en: a front page lying open beside a cup
branches.cn: 摊在杯子旁边的头版

branches.en: a coin handed over for one copy
branches.cn: 买一份报纸递出的一枚硬币

branches.en: a newsroom full of ringing phones
branches.cn: 电话响个不停的编辑部

branches.en: the same sheets as a product and as one purchase
branches.cn: 同样的纸张，既是产品，也是一次购买

branches.en: a copy in a hand and the office that made it
branches.cn: 手里的一份报纸与做出它的报馆

intro.en: The word is a compound of news and paper, and its family keeps pairing the report with print, sellers and the people who make it.
intro.cn: 这个词是 news 与 paper 的复合，词族不断把报道与印刷、售卖者和制作的人配在一起。

latinIntro.en: Latin papyrus names the reed that became paper, and it is the one reliable Latin ancestor behind this compound.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 papyrus 指后来变成纸的那种芦苇，是这个复合词背后唯一可靠的拉丁来源。

items.meaning: material made for writing and printing
the reed used as writing material
the cheap paper used for newspapers
a man who works for a newspaper

latinEntries.meaning: the papyrus reed used as writing material
latinEntries.meaningCN: 用作书写材料的纸莎草

definition_zh: 报摊；书报亭；报刊零售处；报摊零售价
definition_en: a small open booth or metal frame on a pavement where newspapers and magazines are sold
core_image: 街角铁架上整排报纸夹在木夹子里，最上面一份还翻开着
scene: 天刚亮，街角的铁架上已经夹好一排报纸，摊主把硬币盒摆到前排。The newsstand opens before the first bus passes.
sceneCN: 这里 newsstand 是「街头报摊」（第 1 个义项：在街边卖报纸杂志的摊位）；句意为报摊在第一班公交车经过之前就开了门。图中可辨识物件：铁架、木夹子、硬币盒。

pos.zh: 报摊；书报亭；报刊零售处

derivatives.zh: newsstand 的前一个构件，源自古英语 neowe（新的）的复数 neowes，义为「新闻；消息」
newsstand 的后一个构件，源自古英语 stondan（站立），义为「摊位；架子」
由 news 与 paper 复合而成，义为「报纸」
由 news 与 agent（经营者）复合而成，义为「报刊经销商；报刊店」

senses.title: A street stand that sells papers
senses.definition: a small open booth or metal frame on a pavement where newspapers and magazines are sold
senses.definitionCN: 人行道上出售报纸和杂志的小型敞开摊位或金属架
senses.example: He bought a paper at the newsstand near the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他在车站附近的报摊买了一份报纸。
senses.why: The compound puts the goods in front of the place: news names the printed reports, and stand names the frame that holds them at eye level, so the word marks a spot defined by what it displays.
senses.whyCN: 这个复合词把货物摆在地点前面：news 指印出来的新闻，stand 指把报纸架到视线高度的架子，所以这个词标记的是一个由「摆什么」来定义的位置。

senses.title: The price of a copy bought on the street
senses.definition: the full price charged for a single copy at a stand, as opposed to the lower rate offered to subscribers
senses.definitionCN: 在摊上买一份所付的全价，与提供给订户的较低价格相对
senses.example: The magazine costs less by subscription than at newsstand price.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志订阅价比报摊零售价低。
senses.why: Once a stand counts as a recognised place of sale, its price turns into a measuring stick, so publishers quote the newsstand price to set the ordinary buyer's cost against the subscriber's saving.
senses.whyCN: 报摊一旦算作公认的售卖点，它的价格就变成一把尺子，因此出版方用「报摊价」把普通买者付的钱与订户省下的钱放在一起对照。

senses.title: A single copy sold from a stand
senses.definition: one physical copy of a publication bought from a stand rather than received through delivery
senses.definitionCN: 从摊上买到、而不是通过投递收到的那一份实物刊物
senses.example: Collectors hunt for the newsstand copy with the early cover.
senses.exampleCN: 收藏者专门找那种封面是早期版本的报摊零售本。
senses.why: Because the stand sells units one at a time, the word slips from the place to the object handed across the counter, marking the copy that never travelled by post.
senses.whyCN: 因为报摊是一份一份地卖，这个词就从地点滑到柜台递出的东西，专指那本没有走过邮路的本子。

senses.title: The trade of keeping a stand open
senses.definition: the daily business of ordering stock, opening early and selling papers from a fixed pitch
senses.definitionCN: 每天进货、早早开张、在固定点位卖报的营生
senses.example: Running a newsstand means being at the corner before dawn.
senses.exampleCN: 经营报摊意味着天没亮就得守在街角。
senses.why: A stand is also a way of earning a living, so the same noun covers the furniture and the livelihood standing behind it, since a fixed pitch and a daily routine belong to both.
senses.whyCN: 报摊同时也是一种谋生方式，所以同一个名词既指那件家什，也指撑在它背后的生计，因为固定的点位与每天的作息同属两者。

intro.en: Newsstand is a plain English compound of two common words, and its history is mostly the history of its two halves rather than of a borrowed root.
intro.cn: newsstand 是两个普通英语词拼成的复合词，它的来历主要是两个构件各自的来历，而不是某个借来的词根。

items.en: The first element goes back to a reconstructed root for new, the same source that produced Latin novus and Greek neos.
items.cn: 第一个构件可上溯到一个表示「新」的重构词根，拉丁语 novus 与希腊语 neos 都出自这里。

items.en: Neowe meant new, and its plural neowes, literally new things, became the noun news in Middle English.
items.cn: neowe 意为新的，它的复数 neowes 字面是「一件件新事」，到中古英语变成名词 news。

items.en: Stondan meant to stand, and from it came the noun stand for the place where a person or a thing stands and stays.
items.cn: stondan 意为站立，由它产生名词 stand，指人或物站定、停留的位置。

items.en: The two words were joined for the frame at a street corner that holds papers, a use that dictionaries generally date to the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 两个词被合起来指街角夹放报纸的架子，一般认为这种用法可追到十八世纪。

items.en: Modern English applies the word to the booth, the price printed on a cover and the single copy sold there, and it stays on even where a machine replaces the stand.

normalIntro.en: The compound is transparent, news on a stand; what is worth remembering is how each half grew and how the price and the copy took the name of the place.
normalIntro.cn: 这个复合词是透明的：架子上的新闻。值得记住的是两个构件各自怎么长成，以及价格和单份刊物如何借用了这个地点的名字。

normal.en: News began as the plural of new, so it once meant new things rather than a mass of reports.
normal.cn: news 起初是 new 的复数，本来指一件件新事，而不是一堆报道。

normal.en: Stand is the noun from the verb to stand, so a newsstand is the frame that stands and waits for buyers.
normal.cn: stand 是从动词「站立」来的名词，所以报摊就是站在那儿等买主的架子。

normal.en: English often names a shop by what it displays rather than by who owns it, which is why this word begins with news.
normal.cn: 英语常按陈列的东西而不是按主人来给店铺命名，所以这个词以 news 开头。

normal.en: The price printed on a cover is called the newsstand price because that is where the full rate is charged.
normal.cn: 封面上印的价格叫「报摊价」，就是因为在那里收的是全价。

normal.en: A newsstand copy is the opposite of a delivered copy, so the word can jump from the furniture to the paper in your hand.
normal.cn: 报摊零售本与投递到家的本子相对，所以这个词能从架子跳到手里的报纸。

abstract.en: A stand is furniture, a price and a trade at once, because one fixed spot can support all three.
abstract.cn: 报摊同时是家具、价格和营生，因为同一个固定点位能撑起这三样东西。

abstract.en: The word puts the goods before the place, a quiet admission that a stall exists only for what it can show.
abstract.cn: 这个词把货物放在地点之前，等于坦白：摊位只为它能摆出来的东西而存在。

abstract.en: When a machine replaces the stand, the old word survives on the price and the copy, which is how places outlive their furniture.
abstract.cn: 当机器取代了摊位，旧词仍留在价格和单份刊物上，地点就是这样比它的家什活得更久。

definition_en: in a way that pleases or satisfies; with care and neatness; in a polite and proper manner; or with a fine judgement of detail
core_image: 桌布铺得平直，杯沿擦得亮，勺子摆成一条线
scene: 客人还没到，主人把桌布重新铺了一遍，杯沿一只只擦亮。She arranged the cups nicely along the edge of the cloth.
sceneCN: 这里 nicely 是「整齐精细地」（第 2 个义项：对排列和细节都讲究）；句意为她沿着桌布边沿把杯子摆得很整齐。图中可辨识物件：桌布、杯沿、勺子。

pos.zh: 很好地；令人满意地；整齐精细地；得体地

由 nice 加 -ety 构成，义为「细节；微妙之处」

senses.title: In a pleasing or satisfactory way
senses.definition: in a way that gives pleasure or satisfies the people involved
senses.definitionCN: 以让人愉快或让相关人满意的方式
senses.example: The whole plan worked out nicely in the end.
senses.exampleCN: 整个计划最后顺利办成了。
senses.why: The adverb keeps the approving sense of nice, so it presents the result as one people are glad to accept rather than one that is merely correct.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词保留了 nice 的赞许意味，所以它把结果说成让人乐于接受的样子，而不只是勉强正确。

senses.title: With care, order and precision
senses.definition: with careful attention to arrangement, detail or exactness
senses.definitionCN: 对排列、细节或准确度都用心讲究地
senses.example: She arranged the cups nicely along the edge of the cloth.
senses.exampleCN: 她沿着桌布边沿把杯子摆得很整齐。
senses.why: The older sense of nice was delicate and precise, and the adverb keeps that craft sense whenever the subject is how something is placed or made.
senses.whyCN: nice 的旧义是精细、讲究，所以只要话题落在东西怎么摆、怎么做，这个副词就仍带着手艺的意味。

senses.title: In a polite and proper manner
senses.definition: in a way that shows good manners and respect for other people
senses.definitionCN: 表现出良好教养和对他人尊重的方式
senses.example: The children behaved nicely while the guests were there.
senses.exampleCN: 客人来的时候孩子们举止很得体。
senses.why: Because the word approves of what fits a situation, it can judge behaviour as fitting, and politeness is the most social kind of fitting.
senses.whyCN: 因为这个词赞许「合乎场合」的东西，它就能用来评判举止是否合宜，而礼貌正是最社会化的合宜。

senses.title: With a fine judgement of degree or timing
senses.definition: with a delicate sense of degree, timing or tone, so that the effect is exactly what was wanted
senses.definitionCN: 在分寸、时机或语气上把握得细，使效果恰好合乎所需
senses.example: The pause was nicely judged, just long enough to let the joke land.
senses.exampleCN: 那个停顿拿捏得刚好，正好够让笑话落地。
senses.why: Precision and approval meet here: a nicely judged detail is at once exact and pleasing, which is why writers use the adverb for timing and tone rather than for size.
senses.whyCN: 精细与赞许在这里汇合：拿捏得当的细节既准确又讨喜，所以写作者用它修饰时机和语气，而不修饰大小。

intro.en: Nicely is the adverb of nice, a Latin word for ignorance that French and English slowly turned into praise.
intro.cn: nicely 是 nice 的副词形式；nice 这个拉丁词原本指无知，经法语和英语慢慢变成了赞许。

items.en: Nescius meant not knowing, built from ne-, not, and scire, to know, so the word began as a remark about ignorance.
items.cn: nescius 意为不知道的，由否定成分 ne- 与 scire（知道）构成，所以这个词起点是一句关于无知的评语。

items.en: Old French nice meant foolish, simple or silly, and it carried that judgement across the Channel.
items.cn: 古法语 nice 意为愚笨的、头脑简单的，把这层贬评带过了海峡。

items.en: Middle English nice still meant foolish or wanton, a long way from the compliment it gives today.
items.cn: 中古英语的 nice 仍指愚笨、放纵，与今天这层夸奖相距很远。

items.en: In the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries the adjective moved through fussy and delicate to refined and precise, and the adverb nicely followed the same path.
items.cn: 十六、十七世纪间，这个形容词从「挑剔、纤巧」转到「精致、准确」，副词 nicely 也走了同一条路。

items.en: Modern English keeps the approving senses of pleasant, careful and proper, while the old sense of foolish has disappeared.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了「愉快、细致、得体」这些赞许义，而「愚笨」的旧义已经消失。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words on the same Latin stem of knowing; the near-meaning group collects other adverbs of doing something well.
note.cn: 形近组收同一「知道」拉丁词干上的词；近义组收其他表示把事情做好的副词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin adjective of ignorance turned into an English adverb by -ly, and its family still carries both the old judgement and the modern approval.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中表示「无知」的形容词，经 -ly 变成英语副词；它的词族仍同时带着旧日的贬评与今天的赞许。

normal.en: The Latin root is ne plus scire, not to know, so nice once meant ignorant and the praise arrived much later.
normal.cn: 拉丁词根是 ne 加 scire，即「不知道」，所以 nice 曾经指无知，夸奖的意思来得很晚。

normal.en: The suffix -ly only turns an adjective into an adverb, so nicely does whatever nice does, applied to the verb.
normal.cn: 词尾 -ly 只是把形容词变成副词，所以 nicely 做的事就是 nice 做的事，只不过用在动词上。

normal.en: Niceness names the quality and nicety names a fine detail, showing one stem serving both approval and precision.
normal.cn: niceness 指性质，nicety 指细部，可见同一词干同时服务于赞许与精确。

normal.en: Work out nicely is the usual pattern for a result that ends better than expected.
normal.cn: work out nicely 是固定模式，指结果比预想的要好。

normal.en: The word can modify a pause or a judgement because its old sense of delicate still survives in careful writing.
normal.cn: 这个词能修饰停顿或判断，因为「纤巧」的旧义在讲究的文笔里仍然活着。

abstract.en: A word that began as an insult about ignorance now hands out praise, a reminder that approval is often only a fashion away from contempt.
abstract.cn: 一个从「无知」的贬语开始的词如今用来夸人，提醒人：赞许与轻蔑之间常常只隔一阵风气。

abstract.en: Nicely sits between correct and pleasant, describing things that are right in a way people enjoy.
abstract.cn: nicely 站在「正确」与「愉快」之间，形容那些对得让人喜欢的事。

abstract.en: Because it approves of fit, it can judge a pause as easily as a table setting, which shows how one adverb can measure tact.
abstract.cn: 因为它赞许「合宜」，它能评判一个停顿，也能评判一桌摆设，说明一个副词也能衡量分寸。

definition_zh: 侄女；外甥女；姻亲的侄女
definition_en: the daughter of one's brother or sister, or of one's spouse's brother or sister
core_image: 饭桌边一个女孩被长辈塞了红包，笑着往口袋里收
scene: 过年时，长辈把红包塞给桌边那个女孩，她低头笑着收进兜里。My niece stayed by the table until the sweets were gone.
sceneCN: 这里 niece 是「侄女」（第 1 个义项：兄弟姐妹的女儿）；句意为我的侄女一直守在桌边，直到糖都吃完了。图中可辨识物件：饭桌、红包、糖盘。

senses.title: The daughter of one's brother or sister
senses.definition: the female child of one's own brother or sister
senses.definitionCN: 自己兄弟或姐妹的女儿
senses.example: My niece stayed by the table until the sweets were gone.
senses.exampleCN: 我的侄女一直守在桌边，直到糖都吃完了。
senses.why: Latin neptis named exactly this corner of the family, a sibling's daughter, and English kept the narrow sense instead of letting the word mean any young girl.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 neptis 指的正是家谱上这一格：兄弟姐妹的女儿；英语保留了这个窄义，没有让它变成「任何小女孩」的通称。

senses.title: The daughter of one's spouse's sibling
senses.definition: the female child of a husband's or wife's brother or sister
senses.definitionCN: 丈夫或妻子的兄弟、姐妹的女儿
senses.example: His niece by marriage came to the wedding with her own children.
senses.exampleCN: 他妻子那边的侄女带着自己的孩子来参加婚礼。
senses.why: Marriage stretches the same relation sideways, and because English marks the tie rather than the blood, the daughter of a spouse's sibling enters the family under the same word.
senses.whyCN: 婚姻把同一种关系横向拉开；英语标记的是亲属关系而不是血缘，所以配偶兄弟姐妹的女儿也用同一个词进到家里来。

senses.title: A young female relative raised in one's household
senses.definition: a young female relative who lives under one's care, as in older family letters
senses.definitionCN: 旧时家信中指由自己照养的年轻女性亲属
senses.example: The letters call her his niece, though she was the orphan he brought up.
senses.exampleCN: 信里称她为他的侄女，虽然她其实是他抚养长大的孤儿。
senses.why: Households once took in orphaned or poor young relatives, and the word followed the girl into the house, so a guardian could write of his ward as his niece.
senses.whyCN: 旧时家庭会收留失去父母或家境困难的年轻亲属，这个词就跟着女孩进了家门，于是监护人也能把自己的被监护人写作侄女。

intro.en: Niece came to English from Latin by way of French, and it has stayed a narrow label for one branch of the family tree.
intro.cn: niece 由拉丁语经法语进入英语，一直只做家谱某一支的窄标签。

items.en: Neptis meant a brother's or sister's daughter, and it could also stretch to a granddaughter.
items.cn: neptis 指兄弟姐妹的女儿，也可以延伸到孙女。

items.en: The related noun nepos meant a grandson or a descendant, and it is the root behind the later word for favouring one's relatives.
items.cn: 与之相关的名词 nepos 指孙子或后代，它正是后来表示「偏袒亲属」那个词的源头。

items.en: Old French kept the family sense in the form niece and passed it to English after the Norman period.
items.cn: 古法语以 niece 这一形式保留了这层亲属含义，并在诺曼时期之后传给英语。

items.en: Middle English used niece for a sibling's daughter, while cousin still covered a much wider range of kin.
items.cn: 中古英语用 niece 指兄弟姐妹的女儿，而 cousin 那时还覆盖着范围大得多的亲属。

items.en: Modern English pairs niece with nephew for the two children of a sibling and adds the in-law relation without changing the word.
items.cn: 现代英语把 niece 与 nephew 配成一对，分别指兄弟姐妹的两个孩子，并在不改词形的情况下加上姻亲那一层。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the matching kinship word and two words that only share the spelling; the near-meaning group collects other labels on the family tree.
note.cn: 形近组收与之配对的亲属词，以及只是拼写相近的两个词；近义组收家谱上的其他称谓。

entries.definitionCN: 兄弟姐妹的儿子，与 niece 配对的男性称谓。

entries.definition: Pleasant or agreeable; it only looks close to niece and its Latin root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 令人愉快的；只是与 niece 拼写相近，拉丁词根不同。

normalIntro.en: The word is a narrow Latin label for a sibling's daughter that French carried into English, and its small family includes nephew and nepotism.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语中给「兄弟姐妹的女儿」的窄标签，经法语带入英语；它的小词族还包括 nephew 与 nepotism。

normal.en: Latin neptis named a sibling's daughter and sometimes a granddaughter, so the word never meant any girl, only a related one.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 neptis 指兄弟姐妹的女儿，有时也指孙女，所以这个词从不指随便哪个女孩，只指有亲缘的那一个。

normal.en: Nephew is the matching word for a boy, and the pair comes from the same Latin family of kinship terms.
normal.cn: nephew 是配对的男性词，这一对都出自拉丁语同一族亲属称谓。

normal.en: The final e is silent, so niece rhymes with peace and not with nice.
normal.cn: 词尾的 e 不发音，所以 niece 与 peace 押韵，而不是与 nice。

normal.en: Great-niece adds one generation, being the daughter of a niece or a nephew.
normal.cn: great-niece 多出一代，指侄女或侄子的女儿。

normal.en: Nepotism comes from the same Latin root for descendant, which shows how far a family word can travel.
normal.cn: nepotism 出自同一个表示「后代」的拉丁词根，可见一个亲属词能走多远。

abstract.en: A word kept for one exact corner of the family tree shows how carefully English labels kinship.
abstract.cn: 一个只守在家谱某一格的词，说明英语给亲属关系贴标签有多仔细。

abstract.en: Because niece marks the relation and not the blood, marriage can hand the title to a new person without changing the word.
abstract.cn: 因为 niece 标记的是关系而非血缘，婚姻能把这一称谓交给新的人，而词本身毫无变化。

abstract.en: The silent e and the long vowel make niece sound like peace, a small accident that memory can put to use.
abstract.cn: 不发音的 e 与长元音让 niece 听起来像 peace，这个小巧合正好可以拿来记。

examples.en: My niece stayed by the table until the sweets were gone.

examples.en: He drove his niece to school every morning that winter.
examples.cn: 那个冬天他每天早上送侄女上学。

examples.en: She is not my daughter but my niece, the child of my younger sister.
examples.cn: 她不是我女儿，是我的外甥女，我妹妹的孩子。

root: 拉丁语 neptis（兄弟姐妹的女儿，也可指孙女）经古法语 niece 进入英语；与 nephew 同出一系，nepotism 亦源自拉丁语 nepos（后代）。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is a sibling's daughter; the second sense reaches the same relation by marriage, and the third follows a young relative into the household.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是兄弟姐妹的女儿；第二个义项由婚姻抵达同一层关系，第三个义项则跟着一个年轻亲属进了家门。

pos.zh: 夜晚；夜间；晚上

derivatives.zh: 由 night 加 -ly 构成，义为「每夜的；每晚」
由 night 与 fall（落下）复合而成，义为「天黑；入夜」
由 mid（中间）与 night 复合而成，义为「午夜」
由 night 与 life 复合而成，义为「夜生活」

senses.title: The dark hours between sunset and sunrise
senses.definition: the period of darkness that begins at sunset and ends at sunrise
senses.definitionCN: 从日落开始到日出结束的那一段黑暗时间
senses.example: The streets are empty at night.
senses.exampleCN: 夜里街上空无一人。
senses.why: The Old English noun named the dark half of the day, and the word has kept that simple division of the clock ever since.
senses.whyCN: 古英语的这个名词指的就是一天中黑暗的那一半，这个词至今仍守着钟面上这条简单的分界。

senses.title: A night spent asleep
senses.definition: the stretch of rest that a person gets between going to bed and waking
senses.definitionCN: 从上床到醒来之间那一段休息的时间
senses.example: She had a good night and woke up rested.
senses.exampleCN: 她睡了个好觉，醒来精神很好。
senses.why: Because the dark hours are the hours of sleep, the same word names the rest itself, so a good night is counted in hours slept rather than in anything seen.
senses.whyCN: 因为黑暗的那些小时正是睡觉的时辰，同一个词就用来指这段休息本身，所以「好的一夜」是按睡了多少小时来算，而不是按看见了什么。

senses.title: An evening given to an event
senses.definition: an evening set aside for a performance, a match or a social occasion
senses.definitionCN: 为演出、比赛或社交活动专门留出的那个晚上
senses.example: The opening night drew a full house.
senses.exampleCN: 首演之夜座无虚席。
senses.why: An event held after dark borrows the name of the time it fills, so the word can mean an evening handed over to a show or a game.
senses.whyCN: 天黑之后举办的活动会借用它所占据的时段的名字，所以这个词能指交给演出或比赛的那个晚上。

senses.title: The moment darkness falls
senses.definition: the point at which daylight ends and darkness comes down
senses.definitionCN: 白昼结束、黑暗降临的那一刻
senses.example: The light faded and night came down over the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 光线退去，夜幕落到山谷上方。
senses.why: Since the same noun can name a period and its edge, it also marks the arrival of darkness, which is why a sentence can say that night came down.
senses.whyCN: 同一个名词既能指一段时期，也能指它的边缘，所以它也标记黑暗的到来，这才有「夜幕落下」这样的句子。

senses.title: A time of gloom or trouble
senses.definition: a stretch of sorrow, fear or hardship felt as long and heavy as the dark hours
senses.definitionCN: 像黑夜一样漫长沉重的悲伤、恐惧或艰难时光
senses.example: The family went through a long night of worry before the results came.
senses.exampleCN: 结果出来之前，这家人熬过了一段漫长的担忧。
senses.why: Darkness has long served as a figure for trouble, so a night can stand for any spell of fear or grief that feels as though the light will never return.
senses.whyCN: 黑暗自古就被用来比喻困境，所以 night 能指任何一段恐惧或悲伤的时光，仿佛光再也不会回来。

intro.en: Night is one of the oldest words English owns, an Old English noun still close to its Germanic shape and related to Latin nox.
intro.cn: night 是英语里最古老的词之一，这个古英语名词至今仍贴近它的日耳曼语形态，并与拉丁语 nox 同源。

items.en: A reconstructed root usually written nokwt- stands behind the word in many Indo-European languages, though scholars still argue about its exact shape.
items.cn: 许多印欧语系语言中这个词背后都有一个通常写作 nokwt- 的重构词根，不过学者对它的确切形态仍有争论。

items.en: The Germanic noun nahts gave Old English its word and also stands behind German Nacht.
items.cn: 日耳曼语名词 nahts 给了古英语这个词，也是德语 Nacht 的来处。

items.en: Niht named the dark part of the day and already formed compounds such as nihtlic, the ancestor of nightly.
items.cn: niht 指一天中黑暗的部分，并已构成 nihtlic 这样的复合词，那是 nightly 的前身。

items.en: Middle English kept the spellings niht and night, and the gh stopped being pronounced, leaving the long vowel heard today.
items.cn: 中古英语保留 niht 与 night 两种写法，后来 gh 不再发音，只留下今天听到的长元音。

items.en: Modern English uses night for the dark hours, for an evening event and for a time of sorrow, while the gh in the spelling is a silent relic.
items.cn: 现代英语用 night 指黑暗的时段、某个活动的晚上以及悲伤的时期，而拼写里的 gh 是一块沉默的遗迹。

note.en: The look-alike group collects the homophone and the compounds built with this noun; the near-meaning group collects other words for the dark part of the day.
note.cn: 形近组收同音词与用这个名词构成的复合词；近义组收其他表示一天中黑暗时段的词。

entries.definition: A mounted soldier of the Middle Ages; it sounds exactly like night but comes from a different Old English word.
entries.definitionCN: 中世纪的骑马武士；与 night 读音完全相同，却出自另一个古英语词。

entries.definition: Happening or done every night.
entries.definitionCN: 每夜发生或做的。

entries.definition: The middle of the night, twelve o'clock at night.
entries.definitionCN: 夜的正中，夜间十二点。

entries.definition: A small brown bird famous for singing at night.
entries.definitionCN: 因夜间鸣唱而闻名的小型褐色鸟；夜莺。

entries.definition: The part of the day between afternoon and bedtime.
entries.definitionCN: 下午与就寝之间的那段时间；傍晚。

entries.definition: The darker stage of twilight, just before night.
entries.definitionCN: 暮色中最暗的阶段，紧挨着夜晚之前。

entries.definition: The absence of light, the quality that defines the night.
entries.definitionCN: 没有光的状态，正是夜晚之所以为夜的性质。

entries.definition: The period of the night, used as a plain label for the dark hours.
entries.definitionCN: 夜间的时段，用作指黑暗时间的平实说法。

normalIntro.en: The word is an old Germanic noun of night that English kept almost unchanged, with a silent gh in the spelling and a large family of compounds around it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个古老的日耳曼语「夜」名词，英语几乎原样保留，拼写里有个不发音的 gh，周围还有一大族复合词。

normal.en: The gh in the spelling was once a throaty sound, and it went silent while the vowel lengthened.
normal.cn: 拼写里的 gh 曾经是一个喉咙里的音，后来它不响了，元音反而变长。

normal.en: Night and knight sound the same today, though one is a time and the other a rider.
normal.cn: night 与 knight 今天读音相同，但一个是时间，一个是骑马的人。

normal.en: The -ly of nightly means every night, the same ending that appears in daily and weekly.
normal.cn: nightly 里的 -ly 表示「每夜」，与 daily、weekly 用的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: Midnight is simply the middle of the night, built the same way as midday.
normal.cn: midnight 就是夜的正中，构词方式与 midday 一样。

normal.en: German Nacht and Latin nox descend from the same old root, which is why night turns up across so many languages.
normal.cn: 德语 Nacht 与拉丁语 nox 出自同一个古老词根，所以「夜」在许多语言里都有相似的影子。

abstract.en: A word for the dark half of the clock becomes a word for an evening out and for a spell of grief, because darkness measures time in more than one way.
abstract.cn: 一个指钟面暗半边的词，又成了外出的一晚和一段悲伤的时光，因为黑暗可以用不止一种方式计量时间。

abstract.en: Night and knight are twins in sound and strangers in meaning, a reminder that spelling keeps an old history the mouth has dropped.
abstract.cn: night 与 knight 声音上是双胞胎，意义上却是陌路人，提醒人拼写保存着口腔早已丢掉的旧历史。

abstract.en: Every night is both a period and a beginning, which is why the same noun can mean the dark hours and the moment they arrive.
abstract.cn: 每一个夜晚既是一段时期，也是一个开端，所以同一个名词既能指黑暗的时段，也能指它降临的那一刻。

root: 古英语 niht，源自日耳曼语 nahts，更早可追到重构的印欧词根 nokwt-；与德语 Nacht、拉丁语 nox 同源，拼写中的 gh 已不发音。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the dark half of the day; from it come the hours of sleep, an evening given to an event, the moment darkness falls and a figurative time of trouble.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是一天中黑暗的那一半；由此分出来睡觉的那些小时、交给某个活动的晚上、天黑的那一刻，以及比喻意义上的艰难时期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hall light switched off, a street lamp stretching tree shadows into the corner.
core.cn: 核心意象：楼道灯灭下去，路灯把树影拉进屋角。
